## Connection deadlines and abort close: 2026-10-12

The approved socket increment will add an absolute deadline measured by GET-INTERNAL-RUN-TIME, which is the supervisor timer clock.  TCP-STREAM-CONNECT will compute it once from CONNECT-TIMEOUT and pass it through DNS and TCP establishment.  The existing TIMEOUT argument will retain its connection-inactivity meaning.  DNS will propagate network errors rather than converting them into an unknown-host result.

The TCP caller will wait with the remaining deadline and abort on an unsuccessful exit.  Its queued start must check that the caller has not already closed the connection.  Start errors will reach the waiting caller through the existing pending-error slot.  Abort will close the local state and wake readers immediately, then remove timers and dispatch sources on the network queue.  Reset generation will follow [RFC 9293 section 3.10.5](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293.html#section-3.10.5).  A blocked read must check pending errors again after waking.  Tests will cover connection refusal, DNS and connect deadlines, interrupted establishment, EOF, abort during a blocked read, dispatch cleanup, and snapshot invalidation.

SYSTEM/NUMBERS/BIGNUM.LISP BIGNUM-TO-FLOAT takes the leading significand bits with LDB and discards the remainder.  This truncates instead of rounding and prevents the carry that should overflow.  The recommendation is to round the integer significand with ROUND before scaling by the power of two, covering short, single, and double floats through the shared routine.  Tests must cover both signs, even/odd halfway significands, values on either side, and the overflow boundary. Earlier cancellation tests checked only an upper elapsed-time bound, allowing an immediately expired deadline to pass.  Their previous result establishes cleanup behavior but does not establish correct fractional timing.

The recommendation is to convert the timeout to its exact rational value before adding it to the rational clock reading. ## TCP half-close proposal: 2026-10-13

[RFC 9293 sections 3.6.1 and 3.10.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293.html#section-3.6.1) permit sending after the peer has closed its sending direction.  Mezzano enters CLOSE-WAIT on peer FIN, but TCP-SEND accepts only ESTABLISHED.  Its CLOSE-WAIT receive branch also discards acknowledgments.  LAST-ACK currently removes the connection on any ACK, which can discard outstanding data when a late data acknowledgment arrives before the FIN acknowledgment.

The recommendation is to support sending in CLOSE-WAIT, reuse the established-state acknowledgment processing for that state, and retain outstanding data until acknowledged.  Local FIN must consume its sequence number, and closing-state transitions must require acknowledgment of that FIN.  The stream must remain open for output after receive EOF.  This supports TLS close-notify through the existing TCP implementation.  Errors will continue to propagate.

Tests must cover receive EOF followed by successful transmission, acknowledgment and retransmission-queue cleanup, a data-only ACK before the FIN ACK, FIN with duplicate ACK and buffered data, sequence wraparound, ordinary close, abort, and the HTTPS transport checks. ## Long-division type declarations: 2026-10-12

The user approved adding declarations and measuring their effect.  Keep the algorithm, array representation, and speed 3, safety 3, debug 1 policy.  First declare inner-loop indices and computed array indices as fixnums.  Then add bounded types for arithmetic variables and digit reads.  Compare each stage with the recorded preallocated-array benchmark, retaining compiled output and disassemblies on both systems.

For each array access, J is between zero and SIZE-N, and I is between zero and N-1.  Thus J+I, J+N, J+N-1, and the guarded J+N-2 are valid nonnegative array indices.  N-1 and the guarded N-2 are valid divisor indices.  The loop counters can reach their termination values, so their declarations retain the full FIXNUM range.

Let B=2^30.  Digits and quotient estimates lie in [0,B-1].  NUMERATOR lies in [0,B^2-1].  A conservative BORROW bound of [0,B] gives PRODUCT at most B^2-B+1, preserving the unsigned-60-bit bound.  The next borrow is at most B, completing that induction.  DIFFERENCE lies in [-B,B-1].  CARRY is zero or one, and SUM is at most 2B-1.  REMAINDER is nonnegative and bounded by NUMERATOR initially.  Its correction increments occur only below B and leave it below 2B, so unsigned 60 bits suffice.  These bounds support declarations without changing arithmetic.

Timing includes allocations and any collection during verification.  Library loading, certificate parsing, hostname verification, network communication, and TLS key exchange are outside the measured interval.  The first row is the first call after loading and parsing, rather than a cold-machine measurement.  The guest's earlier approximately 11.5-second trace measured this chain verifier. The original Mezzano profile has all 934 verification samples under certificate-signature verification, with 789 under bignum division.  Most samples are in P-384 verification.  The approximately 1.8-second residual calculated earlier assumes only division changes.  Multiplication, shifts, allocation, and normalization in that residual can also improve.

Source inspection identifies three runtime costs.  %%BIGNUM-TRUNCATE uses bit-at-a-time division.  %BIGNUM-LEFT-SHIFT and %BIGNUM-RIGHT-SHIFT perform repeated 32-bit shifts with intermediate allocations.  %%BIGNUM-MULTIPLY-UNSIGNED calls %%BIGNUM-MULTIPLY-STEP for each word product.  That x86-64 assembly primitive allocates a three-word bignum for its 128-bit result.  Reading a full-width word can also allocate a boxed integer.  Compiler optimization of the standalone division loop addresses only part of this work.

The recommendation is to keep the TLS and certificate policy in Lisp and improve the arithmetic primitives through Mezzano's existing Lisp assembler.  Whole-word division, single-pass shifts, and multiplication with register carries and one result allocation address the identified causes.  This is runtime arithmetic work beyond the measured array compiler change.  Meeting 100 milliseconds in Mezzano remains an untested target.  An initial increment should replace repeated-shift allocation and measure the same chain, followed by word multiplication and direct runtime division, with independent arithmetic tests before each installation.

[GMP's low-level interface](https://gmplib.org/manual/Low_002dlevel-Functions) offers word-array operations with caller-provided result storage.  It is the relevant interface if importing arithmetic.  The high-level interface introduces another integer representation and allocation policy.  [GMP's allocation documentation](https://gmplib.org/manual/Custom-Allocation) specifies default malloc/realloc/free use and restrictions on recovery from allocation failure.  No general C foreign-call facility or C-library loader was found in the reviewed Mezzano source.  A GMP port therefore requires calling-convention integration, GC-safe buffer ownership, linked-code loading, and defined error behavior.  Secret-dependent arithmetic also requires operation-specific analysis: GMP distinguishes its secure low-level functions from ordinary operations.

A second alternative is a native complete signature-verification operation.  [BearSSL's ECDSA API](https://bearssl.org/apidoc/bearssl__ec_8h.html) takes a digest, public key, and signature, and returns success or failure.  This boundary would keep certificate parsing, trust, hostname, validity, and chain rules in Lisp while avoiding repeated Lisp/C conversions for each integer operation.  Its [published measurements](https://bearssl.org/speed.html) show 360 P-384 point multiplications per second on a 2012 Xeon with generic i31 code.  Those results support feasibility, but do not measure our guest or a complete certificate check.  Library selection, native integration, and a same-chain benchmark require a separate approved implementation decision.

A complete native TLS port changes a larger part of the system than the measured arithmetic costs require.  The immediate choice is between improving the existing arithmetic primitives and importing a bounded native cryptographic operation.  General compiler development remains useful but has no measured basis for a 115-fold reduction of this complete workload by itself.

## Arithmetic runtime implementation: 2026-10-12

The user approved the existing-assembler arithmetic route and the certificate acceptance test. The first increment extends x86-64 %%BIGNUM-LEFT-SHIFT and %%BIGNUM-RIGHT-SHIFT to any nonnegative fixnum count.  Split the count into a whole-word offset and a residual count modulo 64.  Left shift fills the low words with zeros, copies shifted source words, and emits the final sign word.  Right shift skips whole words, joins adjacent words, and sign-extends the final word.  Counts that discard the complete input return its sign.  Zero count returns the input.  The existing canonicalizer retains its responsibility for shrinking and fixnum conversion.  The x86-64 wrappers call the extended routines once.  ARM64 retains its current implementation.

The ABI requires RBX and R8 through R13 to hold tagged values during collection.  Byte offsets in these registers remain multiples of eight.  Raw words and bit counts use RAX, RCX, RDX, RSI, and RDI.  The original input and count occupy marked stack slots across allocation.  Source pointers are reloaded after allocation.  The reference is [the register and GC metadata specification](../../doc/internals/abi.md).

## Proposed certificate-signature cache: 2026-10-12

The user proposed an in-memory cache with a 24-hour TTL and 1,024-entry limit.  Source review found separate certificate-signature and chain-policy functions in pure-tls.  VERIFY-CERTIFICATE-CHAIN checks dates, critical extensions, issuer relationships, CA/key-usage/path-length constraints, requested purpose, and the current trust roots.  VERIFY-CLIENT-PEER-CERTIFICATE performs hostname verification.  The previous profile identifies certificate-signature verification as the expensive operation.

The recommendation is to cache successful VERIFY-CERTIFICATE-SIGNATURE results.  A key must cover every verification input: signed certificate bytes, signature bytes, signature algorithm and parameters, and the issuer public-key algorithm, parameters, and bytes.  Use the existing SHA-256 implementation to keep keys bounded in size, with an unambiguous encoding of those fields.  Recompute keys from the fields the verifier reads, since parsed certificate structures are mutable.  Chain validation and hostname checks continue on every connection, including resumed sessions.  Configured revocation processing retains its existing path.  The per-handshake CertificateVerify signature remains checked against its current handshake transcript.

[Certificate processing in RFC 5280](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-6.1.3) separates signature verification from current-time validity and revocation checks.  [TLS CertificateVerify in RFC 8446](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446.html#section-4.4.3) authenticates the handshake transcript.  These support placing this cache at the certificate-signature function.

Proposed mechanics: cache positive results for 86,400 elapsed seconds from verification, retain at most 1,024 entries, evict the oldest verification when full, and protect lookup/insertion with the existing Lisp threading library.  Verification runs outside the cache lock.  Cache use discards entries from an earlier Mezzano boot or snapshot restoration.  Loading revised cache/verifier code clears the cache.  Provide an explicit clear operation.  No new dependency is proposed.

Tests would cover hits and cryptographic call counts, expiration, capacity, changed signature inputs, failed verification, concurrent insertion, and boot invalidation.  Existing valid/expired, hostname, trust-store, purpose, chain-constraint, and resumed-session checks must behave the same with a warm cache.  Then measure the same public chain with cold and warm caches and run COMPLETE and CURL through Chromium.  This proposal changes which verification work a cache hit performs and awaits approval under the current design-decision rule.

The user approved implementation.  The cache will use fixed-size SHA-256 keys, an elapsed-time timestamp per success, and oldest-entry eviction.  The current parser represents EC public-key parameters in its algorithm value and RSA-PSS parameters in a plist.  The key covers those parsed representations.  Copy the signature inputs before hashing and verification so both operations use the same bytes.  A generation counter prevents an in-flight verification from inserting after a clear or boot change.  No new dependency is needed.

Source inspection: EQUALP compares vector lengths and active elements, and compares other array dimensions and row-major elements.  EQUALP-HASH omits arrays and numbers, sending both to its constant-zero fallback.  All distinct octet-vector cache keys therefore receive zero.  The cache's signature tests completed in the guest. Recommendation: add value-based numeric hashing and ordered array-content hashing to EQUALP-HASH.  Use one element-hashing path for specialized and general vectors, including strings, so equal representations receive equal hashes.  Vector hashing uses LENGTH and therefore respects fill pointers.  Other arrays include dimensions and row-major elements.  Preserve the existing depth bound.  Normalize finite floats through RATIONAL, matching the runtime's mixed rational/float equality.  Numeric zero, including complex values with a zero imaginary part, must hash consistently.  Handle infinities without calling RATIONAL.

HASH-TABLE already retains its construction-time hash function, but optimized lookup instead calls the current global function.  Use the recorded function in lookup.  Each table then retains the algorithm that placed its entries, including across code replacement and snapshots.  New tables capture the corrected function.  This uses the existing slot and requires no new table representation, registry, migration, or dependency.

Direct guest RPC tests returned completion, 16 documents, and 33 processes.  Fresh Chromium also completed those activities.  Those fresh-session tests did not establish behavior in the user's retained tab.

The Web agent reproduced every reported symptom by expiring its owned session, retaining sessionStorage, and reloading.  Resume returned HTTP 409 with :expired-session and uncertain=false.  The client left connected=false.  SPACE issued no assistance RPC, Return issued no evaluation RPC, Document Examiner remained empty after its rejected lookup, and Peek issued no process request.  The existing New Session menu action restored the functions.  Evidence: /tmp/ui-failure-repro/expired/.  The actual user tab remains unobserved, but this reproduces the reported HTTP status and failures.

Recommendation: use the existing New Session state transition after an explicit :expired-session response, at startup or during an active request.  Archive the former session's request records, preserve input and document history, obtain new guest tokens, and refresh the visible activity.  Prior evaluation and debugger requests retain their original identities and are never submitted through the replacement session.  Other errors retain their existing paths.  The correction adds no dependency.  The Web agent owns the implementation and browser tests.  Required tests include expired startup storage, active-tab expiration, successful completion/evaluation/documents/processes after recovery, preservation of pending records, absence of evaluation replay, and ordinary same-session reconnection.

## Concurrent job release during Web refresh: 2026-10-12

A fresh run of the broad Chromium driver received :released-job during initial refresh while another test cleaned up its own retained jobs.  The page remained connected, but refresh stopped and the driver could not observe its expected startup message.  The run created no evaluation jobs.  Evidence: /tmp/web-recovery-broad-results/failure-session.json and /tmp/web-recovery-broad.log.

The retained protocol lists global job handles, and the browser then reads each job's information and output in separate requests.  Another session can release a job between those reads.  Recommendation: a :released-job response while refreshing that particular job removes its local entry through the same operation used after a successful release, then continues the remaining jobs.  Other errors propagate.  This handles the guest's explicit deletion result and adds no retry, dependency, or protocol operation.  Test a live release before information and before output, preserving another completed job and Listener operation.

## Clear All: 2026-10-12

The user requested one command to delete retained evaluation and debugger clutter and then instructed implementation.  Clear All captures existing evaluation jobs, terminates running evaluation threads through the supervisor's existing termination operation, waits for their unwind cleanup, and releases their retained data and closed debugger stops.  The command excludes its own job and preserves submissions accepted after its target snapshot.  Its retained result supports original-request recovery.  The browser clears evaluation output, input history, and request/debugger records when that result returns.  Document Examiner viewers and bookmarks retain their documentation state.

Termination runs outside the service mutex.  Existing UNWIND-PROTECT cleanup closes debugger stops and evaluation streams.  Release retains used job names, preserving rejection of replay after deletion.  Active debugger stops in threads outside the evaluation service require separate debugger control and are reported.  Tests must cover a returned job, interactive input wait, an active debugger stop, unwind cleanup, new jobs after target capture, repeated command requests, and browser history after reload.

## Bounded monitor output: 2026-10-12

The initial monitor batch copied each retained job's complete unread output.  SWANK's six-digit hexadecimal message header permits at most 16,777,215 encoded bytes.  A sufficiently large retained output could therefore prevent the whole monitor response from returning, including the data needed to reach the Document Examiner.

Recommendation: share a 65,536-character output budget across unread jobs and use the existing ranged output reader.  Each row retains its full sampled output length and returns the start and end of the delivered prefix.  The next request supplies those end offsets.  Sort unread rows by supplied offset before distributing the remaining budget among the remaining rows, with at least one character while budget remains.  Short rows leave their unused share for later rows.  Response rows retain their original order.  This also permits progress when unread rows outnumber the budget without introducing a retained cursor.  The budget bounds output text.  Metadata and printed values remain subject to the protocol message-size limit.

Required tests: Unicode offsets and exact reconstructed output, invalid offsets, a growing output alongside a short job, more unread jobs than a small test budget, no handle growth, released-object omission, and Listener and Document Examiner responsiveness while output remains.  The browser must append partial prefixes and render a pathname presentation only after all its characters arrive.  A completed evaluation can still have unread output.

This distinguishes completed execution from incomplete output transfer.  Tests must split Unicode text and presentation ranges across replies and reject invalid offsets.

## Clear All concurrency and startup review: 2026-10-12

Source review identified three cancellation cases absent from the initial tests.  Concurrent clearing jobs can include each other in their target snapshots.  A termination delivered before RUN-EVALUATION-JOB establishes unwind cleanup can leave a dead job marked running.  A clearing command can overwrite package and pathname changes published by the preceding Listener job during its unwind.  The terminated count also counted requests whose target had already returned.

Recommendation: serialize clearing with one supervisor mutex acquired outside the service mutex, then capture job/thread pairs and stops under the service mutex.  Wait until a captured running job has established its interrupt-ready boundary, or has completed, before requesting termination outside that mutex.  Join captured threads without the service mutex and count the termination result returned by THREAD-JOIN.  Keep a waiting clearing job foothold-enabled so an earlier clear can terminate and join it.  A job accepted after the target snapshot survives that clear.  Skip package/pathname publication by the Clear All control command, which changes neither setting.

The reviewed mechanisms are WITH-SERVICE-LOCK in system/debugger-service.lisp, RUN-EVALUATION-JOB in system/evaluation-service.lisp, and the thread entry, foothold, join, and mutex implementations in supervisor/thread.lisp and supervisor/sync.lisp.  Required tests include cancellation before evaluation entry, a clearing job blocked on the clear mutex, normal completion before a termination request, Listener package/pathname preservation, existing unwind cleanup, and later submissions.  Global tests require a coordinated guest window because their purpose is to delete retained evaluations.

After the parser correction, all 11 malformed-input browser cases returned :invalid-private-document and left subsequent topic queries usable.  A missing unique pathname then reproduced HTTP 502 with uncertain=true from MEZZANO.FILE-SYSTEM:SIMPLE-FILE-ERROR.  Evidence: /tmp/document-commands-fourth/failure-api.json.  The test removed its owned file and released its 13 jobs and session.

Recommendation: classify FILE-ERROR and remaining STREAM-ERROR conditions during private-document reading as :private-document-io-error, retaining the requested pathname and original condition.  Reader syntax and truncated input remain :invalid-private-document through the inner handlers.  Missing topics retain :missing-topic.  Other condition types propagate.  Test a missing file through the browser and verify rejection, unchanged viewer, subsequent successful query, and cleanup.

## Confirmed snapshot inconsistency: 2026-10-13

Read-only decoding of the failed image, using the image-manip.lisp format and instance layout, found the invalid state already on disk.  Thread 0x17b5be9 is cl-cancel-deadline-timer.  Its saved state is :RUNNABLE, queue-next is NIL, and queue-prev is run-queue predecessor 0x16d66f9.  Its saved wait-item is deadline-timer-condition at 0xe3fc29, whose saved head and tail both still point to that same thread.  The CV's wired page 0xe3f000 was copied before thread page 0x17b5000.  Boot consumes this contradictory snapshot rather than creating it.

SNAPSHOT-COPY-WIRED-AREA disables interrupts on its own CPU only.  Its existing FIXME records that stopping the world is insufficient to suspend the other CPUs.  Ordinary threads stop, but the other CPU's idle loop reenables interrupts.  A PIT timeout can therefore remove a CV waiter and make it runnable while those wired pages are being copied.  The saved older CV and newer thread match that sequence.

Required correction: quiesce interrupt handling on every other CPU for the wired-copy interval, using the existing CPU coordination mechanisms where possible.  Disabling a library timer or reducing QEMU's CPU count would leave the snapshot defect.  Review the rendezvous, lock ordering, and release path before implementing the exclusion.  Test a native timed CV waiter across a two-CPU snapshot, repeat restoration under timer activity, and complete the retained-browser and HTTPS checks.

The final UI backend recompiled and loaded in the diagnostic guest.  The guest Clear All suite passed again, including early entry, concurrent clearing, termination counts, input/debugger waits, cleanup, later submissions, and Listener defaults.  It released the old snapshot's retained evaluations as part of the explicitly global test.  Evidence: ui-backend-reload.log and ui-reload-clear-all.log.

## Snapshot CPU exclusion correction: 2026-10-13

Review of supervisor/x86-64/cpu.lisp and supervisor/thread.lisp supports reusing the existing TLB-shootdown rendezvous to suspend peer CPUs during wired copying.  BEGIN-TLB-SHOOTDOWN parks peers inside interrupt-disabled handlers.  The snapshot caller already holds the VM write lock and has stopped ordinary threads, which serializes this operation against page-table changes.  The snapshot worker cannot migrate while waiting because IRQ preemption excludes both the world-stopping thread and supervisor-priority threads.

Recommendation: on x86-64, begin that rendezvous before the existing local WITHOUT-INTERRUPTS copy, then call FINISH-TLB-SHOOTDOWN in UNWIND-PROTECT after restoring local interrupts.  BEGIN must run with local interrupts enabled: an in-flight BSP profiler may be waiting for this CPU's magic-button IPI acknowledgment.  Masking local interrupts before BEGIN could cause the two CPUs to wait for each other.  Peer CPUs remain suspended throughout copying.  Boot resets the saved shootdown-in-progress flag before enabling interrupts, and each rendezvous initializes its acknowledgment counter.

This correction uses the existing resident synchronization code and adds no library.  ARM64's corresponding helpers are no-ops, so the implementation and execution claim is x86-64 only.  Retain the scheduler's wake-state assertion.  Test the two-CPU image with a native timed-CV restoration fixture and existing timer activity, including saved queue/thread consistency and the original browser restoration checks.  The reader of the failed image is diagnostic evidence and does not modify it.

## Snapshot exclusion test: 2026-10-13

The scheduler has shared run queues and no inspected thread-affinity API.  A snapshot performed on the timer's BSP would mask PIT interrupts locally even before the correction, so a successful restore alone does not exercise peer exclusion.

Recommendation: install test-only wired observers around the existing BEGIN-TLB-SHOOTDOWN and FINISH-TLB-SHOOTDOWN functions, restricted to the snapshot thread.  Use preallocated wired storage to record copying CPU, BSP identity, PIT IRQ count, runtime counter, and TSC immediately after BEGIN returns and immediately before FINISH.  Require a non-BSP copying CPU, the rendezvous active with zero outstanding acknowledgments, unchanged PIT/runtime counts, and elapsed TSC longer than a PIT interval.  Keep observers free of allocation and printing and restore the original functions after measurement.  Bounded attempts may find a non-BSP run.  A BSP-only run does not establish that case.

The native CV fixture will establish two sleeping, queue-linked waiters with explicit long-lived timers, verify saved relationships before and after restoration, then test notification and timer expiration separately.  Each worker must reacquire its mutex and complete once.  Final assertions check empty queues, disarmed/unlinked timers, joined workers, and cleanup.  Pre-snapshot readiness is distinguished from the exact copying boundary.

The production wired-copy function compiled in Mezzano and loaded with wired allocation.  Its function address lies in the wired function area.  Disassembly places BEGIN before local interrupt masking and FINISH in the outer cleanup after flags restoration.  Evidence: snapshot-cpu-exclusion-load.log and home/snapshot-cpu-exclusion-20261013.disassembly.  No snapshot had run with the correction at this point.

## Proposed COMPLETE keyword interface: 2026-10-13

Status: proposed for user review.  The implementation remains unchanged.

Source review: tools/https/listener.lisp accepts a prompt string and an optional positional model.  LISPM-OPENAI:CREATE-RESPONSE already accepts a Jzon request hash table and returns parsed JSON plus the HTTP request ID.  Reuse that transport and the private key file.  Keep the default model gpt-4.1-nano, store false, and one synchronous POST.

Recommendation:

    (complete input &key (model "gpt-4.1-nano")
                         instructions max-output-tokens temperature top-p
                         reasoning-effort verbosity text-format
                         (timeout 60))

INPUT accepts a prompt string or a nonempty proper list of message property lists, each containing exactly :ROLE and :CONTENT.  Roles are :SYSTEM, :DEVELOPER, :USER, or :ASSISTANT.  Content is a string.  Preserve message order and caller-owned data.  A native vector of Jzon input-item objects also permits caller-managed Responses history and structured content without another recursive conversion format.  Validate the vector and object types locally.  The service validates the item schemas.

MODEL is a nonempty string.  INSTRUCTIONS is a string.  MAX-OUTPUT-TOKENS maps to max_output_tokens, including reasoning tokens, with the documented integer minimum of 16.  TEMPERATURE accepts finite numbers from 0 through 2.  TOP-P accepts finite numbers from 0 through 1.  REASONING-EFFORT maps a documented keyword to reasoning.effort.  VERBOSITY accepts :LOW, :MEDIUM, or :HIGH and maps to text.verbosity.  TEXT-FORMAT is a Jzon hash table for text.format, including JSON Schema configuration.  TIMEOUT is a finite positive duration in seconds using the existing cancellation semantics.

NIL omits an optional API field.  Explicit numeric zero is sent.  Validate arguments before reading the credential or sending a request.  Model-specific API rejections propagate with the existing HTTP condition.  Keep the selected model and requested options on errors.  Replacing the positional model with :MODEL is a proposed source incompatibility.  Update repository callers, tests, and documentation after approval.

Return three values on success: concatenated output text, the parsed response hash table, and the HTTP request ID.  Structured JSON output remains a string in the first value.  The caller can parse it with Jzon.  Retain completed-status checking.  Add a completion condition for incomplete generation, refusal, and missing output text, retaining the response, request ID, reason, and any partial text.  Preserve existing transport and HTTP conditions.  The existing lower-level API continues to serve callers needing arbitrary request fields.  Streaming and tool execution require separate interfaces.

References: [Responses request reference](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/python/resources/responses/methods/create), [text generation and message roles](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/text), and [structured outputs](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs).  The direct documentation fetch returned a placeholder for the generic request reference.  The Python reference and its linked text/reasoning schemas supplied the field definitions.

Required tests after approval:

- [ ] Test message normalization, field encoding, NIL omission, numeric zero, validation, and preservation of caller-owned data.
- [ ] Test ordered text extraction, response/request-ID values, incomplete output, refusal, and missing text with response fixtures.
- [ ] Test prompt and message-history requests, sampling and output limits, schema output, and model rejection through the Web Listener with headless Chromium.
- [ ] Update the HTTPS reference and Document Examiner documentation, then commit and push the tested implementation.

## Tool-call design review: 2026-10-13

Status: recommendations for review.  Runtime implementation remains unchanged.

The initial tool proposal combined an execution loop with claims about recovery that require additional design.  Preserve the existing CREATE-RESPONSE transport and make COMPLETE own a bounded synchronous loop over explicitly supplied Lisp tool objects.  Tools contain a name, description, Jzon argument schema, and function object.  Keep exact name lookup, strict true, and parallel_tool_calls false.  Reject duplicate registration names before sending the first request.  Each callback accepts one parsed JSON object and supplies a Jzon-compatible result.  Application argument checks remain the callback's responsibility.  OpenAI strict mode requires additionalProperties false on every schema object and all properties listed as required, with nullable types for optional values.

Prefer :MAX-TOOL-CALLS, default 8, over the previous :MAX-TOOL-ROUNDS.  With at most one function call per response, N executed calls require at most N+1 model requests.  The last request may return final text.  A further requested call signals a limit condition before callback entry.  Validate response completion, supported output kinds, call count, nonempty call ID, registered name, and JSON-object arguments before invoking a callback.  Refusal and incomplete output signal conditions before tool dispatch.  Repeated call IDs signal a protocol condition before another invocation.  Separate calls with different IDs can still request the same operation.

Record callback entry, returned Lisp value, and encoded result as distinct stages.  A serialization error after the function returns must retain the returned value and original call.  A callback can commit a side effect and then signal an error.  Its effects are then uncertain.  A completed in-memory record cannot establish exactly-once external execution across failure or snapshot restoration.  The proposed initial increment performs no automatic request or callback retry.  Explicit resumption requires a separate API specifying run ownership, deadlines, and which stage may resume.

The Web debugger currently invokes restarts with zero arguments.  Source evidence: system/debugger-service.lisp invokes INVOKE-RESTART with only a restart object, and tools/swank/web/server.py accepts a restart index.  The proposed SUPPLY-TOOL-RESULT restart would require argument-taking or interactive restart support in that API.  Recommendation: retain original tool conditions and their live frames through ordinary signaling.  Support existing inspection and ABORT in this increment.  Keep argument-taking recovery as an explicit debugger feature rather than adding a tool-specific substitute.  HANDLER-CASE around the callback followed by a new ERROR would unwind the original frames and is unsuitable here.

One outer cancellation context must cover normalization, all HTTP requests, and callbacks.  CREATE-RESPONSE currently creates a context per POST.  Its library clamps child deadlines to the parent, so an outer context can provide the operation deadline.  Check cancellation before each request and callback.  Record a callback's returned value before the next cancellation check.  Expiration during a debugger stop continues to count toward that deadline.  Resuming execution after expiration signals cancellation before further requests or callbacks.  Cooperative cancellation cannot bound the return time of arbitrary callback code.

MAX-OUTPUT-TOKENS remains a per-request ceiling.  Under the sequential call limit, the generated-token ceiling is at most (N+1) times that ceiling, when supplied.  Input tokens and tool output sizes require separate accounting.  Report final text, final response, and final HTTP request ID as the first three values.  A fourth per-invocation run record retains ordered responses/request IDs, tool-call stages/results, and summed usage for responses received.  Usage excludes any server work whose reply was lost.  Credential strings and authorization headers are excluded from that record.  Original callback errors remain available to the retained debugger with the run on its live stack.  After unwinding, continued execution is outside the initial API.

Continuation must replay output items in order, including reasoning content and assistant phase, and append each function_call_output under its matching call_id.  Preserve the same instructions, model, schemas, and generation options on each request.  Keep intermediate assistant text in history and return the terminal response's text as COMPLETE's first value.  Caller-owned input and schemas must remain unchanged.

References: [function-call handling](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling#handling-function-calls), [strict schemas](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling#strict-mode), [parallel-call controls](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling#parallel-function-calling), and [reasoning continuation without stored responses](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning#preserve-reasoning-without-stored-responses).  Local review used the current client and debugger sources and the debugger reference.  A first source search used an incorrect debugger path; the implementation is system/debugger-service.lisp.

Tests required before claiming support:

- [ ] Counter tool followed by JSON encoding failure and by continuation HTTP failure: retain the correct call stage and preserve the counter value.
- [ ] Tool side effect followed by a Lisp error: original frames and condition remain inspectable, with ABORT available.
- [ ] Incomplete response, refusal, malformed arguments, unknown name, duplicate ID, unexpected multiple calls, and exhausted call limit: reject before callback entry.
- [ ] Zero-call limit, final request after the last permitted call, and per-request token limits.
- [ ] Expiration during a tool or debugger stop: retain completed work and check cancellation before another operation.
- [ ] Continuation carries instructions, call IDs, output order, reasoning items, and schema definitions without mutating caller data.
- [ ] Guest and headless Chromium execution with final values and intermediate usage/history inspection.

## HTTP trace breakpoint and connection registration: 2026-10-13

The user requested a breakpoint for a subsequent COMPLETE call.  Installed `(trace :break t drakma::default-port)` in the running guest.  Drakma calls DEFAULT-PORT from HTTP-REQUEST before opening the connection for the Responses URL.  Its argument is the URI.  TRACE :BREAK uses Mezzano's existing function wrapper and BREAK support.  `(untrace drakma::default-port)` removes this breakpoint.  The request deadline continues during a stop, so the demonstration should use `:timeout 600`.

The initial installation check incorrectly expected FDEFINITION to return the trace wrapper.  FDEFINITION returns its original function.  Inspection through FUNCTION-REFERENCE-FUNCTION confirmed the installed wrapper and its true break condition.  Aborted and released the failed assertion job.

A headless Chromium evaluation of DEFAULT-PORT reached the retained debugger.  An inspection request then returned HTTP 409 with :CLOSED-CONNECTION.  SWANK's MAKE-CONNECTION queues :ADD-CONNECTION to its sentinel and returns before that message must be handled.  The caller can start request workers while the connection is absent from SWANK::*CONNECTIONS*.  The retained service's CHECK-CONNECTION tests membership in that list and rejects an absent connection as closed.  This ordering permits the observed rejection.  Recommendation: complete connection registration before starting request workers, preserving the sentinel's ownership of the connection list.  This correction requires user approval and remains unimplemented.

Inspected the owned test stop through SWANK, confirmed the trace-break condition, invoked CONTINUE, and checked the returned value 443.  Released its stop, job, and session.  The breakpoint remains armed for the user's call.  Evidence: /tmp/http-breakpoint-web.log and the retained-stop inspection result.  The Web debugger test failed.  No source implementation changed in this increment.

## Interrupting a debugger operation: 2026-10-13

The existing delivery check cancels an interrupt whenever *SERVICE-CURRENT-STOP* is non-NIL.  Consequently a blocked condition printer or interactive restart reader cannot enter a child debugger.  A second request also fails while the original evaluation interrupt remains running.  The approved specification requires recovery from both cases.

Use the existing numbered interrupt requests and supervisor footholds.  Bind a command marker only inside the command's established ABORT restart.  Delivery at a retained stop requires that marker to identify the stop's active command.  A parked command loop still receives :ALREADY-STOPPED.  A nested request captures the preceding running interrupt in its delivery closure.  Finishing or cancelling the nested request restores that preceding record, preserving its result and replay identity.  This requires no new structure layout or separate interruption service.  Job information will report :INTERRUPTIBLE-P from the current command and interrupt state for browser button availability.  Delivery rechecks state on the target thread and respects WITHOUT-FOOTHOLDS.

Tests must interrupt condition printing, an interactive argument read, and a command inside an earlier interruption stop.  They must continue the interrupted operation or abort only that operation, preserve the original stop, reject a second pending request, retain identical-ID replay, restore the preceding interrupt ID, execute cleanup once, and permit subsequent evaluation.  Existing evaluation-interruption tests remain required.  Browser tests must use Interrupt, the resulting child stop, Abort, and continuation.  No live reload will occur during the Web agent's current suite.

## Dead-thread global-list links: 2026-10-13

Source review found that THREAD-FINAL-CLEANUP repairs neighboring list links and the global head but leaves THREAD-GLOBAL-NEXT and THREAD-GLOBAL-PREV on the removed object.  Thread objects use the ordinary instance pointer layout, so the collector follows these slots even when SCAN-THREAD skips the dead thread's stack contents.  A retained dead thread can therefore retain a former neighbor after that neighbor exits.

Recommendation: clear both global-list links after removal while the existing global thread lock is held.  Preserve the thread's own stack and join result for existing inspection and join callers.  Test two adjacent threads, retain the newer thread after it exits, then let the older thread exit.  Before the correction, require the retained thread's next link and a weak pointer to identify the older thread after full GC.  After the correction, require NIL links, collection of the older thread and its stack, stable joins for the retained thread, and intact live-list forward/backward links.  Compile the kernel function with wired allocation and test in Mezzano.  Existing dead objects may still contain links created by the previous implementation.

The first stale-link test panicked in CHECK-LIVE-LIST with Interrupts enabled when they shouldn't be.  The test called WITH-GLOBAL-THREAD-LOCK without disabling interrupts, violating that internal spinlock's calling requirements.  Replaced that direct lock access with the existing ALL-THREADS API.  The revised check verifies membership, absence of dead fixtures, and duplicate-free traversal.  It does not inspect backward links.  No thread-cleanup implementation change had been loaded.  Preserved the console as debugger-thread-test-panic-20261013.log.  The concurrent broad browser run lost its connection at this panic and must rerun after recovery.

Review of every global-list reader found that ALL-THREADS traverses the links without locking.  Clearing a removed thread's next link could truncate a concurrent traversal.  Extend the correction to capture the list into a temporary wired vector under the existing global lock with interrupts disabled, then construct the returned list after releasing the lock.  Allocate and grow that vector before locking.  Retry if concurrent creation exceeds its capacity.  This avoids allocation and pageable storage under the spinlock.  GC traversals already stop ordinary threads, the profiler suspends peer CPUs, and panic traversal is diagnostic.  Test ALL-THREADS during repeated creation and exit, including a list larger than the initial vector capacity.

The corrected test reproduced retention through THREAD-GLOBAL-NEXT after the neighboring thread exited and full GC completed.  Both changed kernel functions compiled at safety 3/debug 1/speed 1 with warnings NIL and failure NIL and loaded into the wired function area.  The positive test then observed NIL links on the retained dead thread, collection of its former neighbor and that neighbor's stack, and unchanged repeated join results. Each captured list contained every waiting fixture and the enumerating thread without duplicates.  Fixture cleanup completed. The restored guest executed the new paging initializer, then panicked with Serial read char not implemented. Its error was No route to host 10.0.2.2, before DHCP installed the replacement interface's routes.  The native debugger attempted input on its output-only serial stream. The first description suggested a newly accepted connection.  Read-only inspection of the paused VM found that the stream in ACCEPT-CONNECTIONS refers to a connection from the previous boot: its boot event is signalled, its state is CLOSED, and its pending error is CONNECTION-STALE.  This distinguishes a restored authentication activation from evidence of a newly accepted connection.  TCP-ACCEPT also lacks stale-connection filtering, but changing that function alone cannot protect an authentication activation already saved after acceptance.

Recommendation: add an explicit WAIT-FOR-ROUTE option to TCP-CONNECT and TCP-STREAM-CONNECT.  When requested, wait on a condition variable associated with the existing route-table mutex until a route is available or the existing connection deadline expires.  ADD-ROUTE notifies waiters under that mutex.  Route waiting, DNS, and TCP establishment share the existing deadline.  Enable this option for remote filesystem connections, including connections without reuse.  Other TCP callers retain immediate NO-ROUTE-TO-HOST behavior.  No polling, fixed startup delay, disabled authentication, or replacement transport is required.

Genera assigns RESUME to the innermost proceed handler, falling back to the innermost restart handler.  Common Lisp's restart objects do not carry that distinction.

Recommendation under standing authorization: implement `:Proceed` using the first captured restart named CL:CONTINUE. Mark the selected default in the restart listing.  This mapping is a documented Common Lisp adaptation, and does not infer that an arbitrary restart is safe to select automatically.

Keep the accepted operation and its argument in the existing numbered command record.  Use the stopped thread's existing interactive reader and command abort boundary.  No structure layout, new transport, or dependency is needed.  Complete this increment before adding explicit Lisp argument forms, whose acceptance and replay require separate source-value handling.

Source review of REBUILD-DEBUG-MAP found that it records an original instruction only when its binding layout is nonempty.  Its following pass interprets a missing entry as an inserted instruction and copies the preceding layout. ## Backend source environments: 2026-10-14

AST conversion emits backend instructions without source environments.  Later passes insert replacements through INSERT-BEFORE and INSERT-AFTER, move existing objects, and change instruction classes.  Register allocation inserts fills, spills, and control-flow edge blocks.  The existing variable debug map identifies storage but cannot identify the lexical scope of each instruction.

Recommendation: add one source-environment slot to BACKEND-INSTRUCTION.  AST conversion supplies the current executable node's environment.  Preserve an explicit known null environment and explicit :UNKNOWN.  New replacement instructions inherit the replaced operation's environment through the existing insertion helpers; moving an initialized instruction retains its environment.  Appending a standalone instruction without AST context records :UNKNOWN.  Prologue and final return instructions outside an AST expression also record :UNKNOWN.

Review control-flow insertions separately.  A branch moved from a target block retains that branch's environment.  Split edge blocks use their predecessor terminator's environment, including register-allocation edge transfers.  Their physical insertion before a target block must not select the target's scope.  Class changes retain the shared slot.

Test null/unknown scope, insertion, movement, class changes, source calls before and after backend lowering and register allocation, nested and inlined scopes, closure compilation, control-flow edges, and compiled execution.  Recompile the edited backend files and representative compiler files in Mezzano, then run the existing compiler and debugger fixtures.  This increment carries compiler metadata.  PC encoding, binding storage identities, compiled-file serialization, and runtime frame evaluation remain work.

A newly constructed instruction leaves the slot unbound until emission or insertion initializes it.  This distinguishes omitted metadata from an explicit NIL or :UNKNOWN without a second flag.  Every linked instruction must have a bound slot.  The fixture checks that invariant before and after backend lowering and register allocation.  The bootstrap defines the new class slot and exports its accessor before compiling the changed files with the current compiler, then loads the compiled files during a coordinated guest window.

## Compiled binding identities: 2026-10-14

Review found that register allocation preserves LEXICAL-VARIABLE identity in its debug map, but both code generators replace that object with DEBUG-VARIABLE-NAME.  Closure layout construction also retains only names.  The encoded location stream consequently cannot distinguish different same-name bindings by identity.  Its delta compressor compares those names.  Frame evaluation must select the binding in the source environment and locate that binding's storage.

Recommendation: give each compiler binding a small shared descriptor containing its display name.  Retain the descriptor in its existing compiler property list, and emit that object wherever the debug records currently contain the binding's name.  A copied binding gets a new descriptor.  A captured binding keeps its descriptor across its functions.  The existing constant pool, object writer, and snapshot mechanisms preserve shared identity.  This avoids a separate numeric ID table and another location encoding.  Runtime decoding will retain the descriptor while exposing the existing display name.  Legacy records without descriptors remain readable and report absent binding identity.

Review every consumer before implementation.  Test same-name nested and disjoint bindings, variable/function namespaces, captured cells, copied/inlined bindings, instruction location changes, native compiled-file save/load, full GC, and existing local inspection.  This increment will preserve storage identity; PC-specific lexical scope records and live frame evaluation remain separate work.  Complete the current backend/browser restoration test before loading this change.

## Remote open after orderly connection closure: 2026-10-14

During Web acceptance the development guest panicked before a new HTTP session could open.  The serial stack identifies SWANK::AUTHENTICATE-CLIENT -> SLIME-SECRET -> remote OPEN -> COMMAND -> READ-PRESERVING-WHITESPACE, which signalled END-OF-FILE.  The native debugger then read its output-only cold stream and panicked with Serial read char not implemented.  The host file-server log ends with four .slime-secret probes and Client closed.  The server has a sixty-second idle timeout and suppresses its client-loop errors, so that log does not establish which condition closed this connection.  The guest's EOF and failing operation are established.

OPEN-USING-HOST already retries its initial, read-only PROBE once on TCP CONNECTION-ERROR.  Orderly TCP receive closure returns EOF rather than that condition.  The zero-length connection check also cannot detect orderly EOF because it requests no input.  Recommendation: include END-OF-FILE in the existing initial-probe retry handler.  Preserve the one-retry bound and keep subsequent file creation/open operations outside that handler. ## Inspector components and modification: 2026-10-14

Recommendation: use one Lisp component enumerator, one checked place writer, and the existing retained command loop.  INSPECT accepts NIL for the primary evaluation-history value or (object-reference start count).  MODIFY accepts (part-reference start count), reads one expression through QUERY-IO with reader evaluation disabled, evaluates it in the selected frame, stores its primary value, and returns a fresh page of the containing object.  Refactor the existing frame evaluator to return raw values before its caller prints them, preserving one history implementation.  DESCRIBE-OBJECT accepts an object reference or NIL; CLEAR-INSPECTION accepts NIL.

Pages return object, title, type, start, end, total, count, and parts.  End is exclusive, count retains the requested size, and start clamps to the observed total if the object shrinks.  Reject negative starts and counts outside 1 through 64 before acceptance.  Each part has label, bound-p, printed value, object reference, and optional writable part reference.  Default count is 32.  Immutable object references retain no raw payload; their stop owns that payload.  Command results retain printed data and references only.  Clear releases inspector retention, while evaluation history or application bindings may independently retain the same objects.

Conses expose CAR/CDR; arrays expose row-major elements, including storage beyond a fill pointer; symbols expose name, package, value, function, and plist; hash tables expose alternating key/value rows; instances expose slots.  Only hash values are writable.  Symbol constants, special-operator or macro function cells, and read-only structure slots have no write action.  Fixed-vector structure fields expose element places instead of copies.  Other object types retain their printed identity and have no component rows in this increment.

A component reference retains its containing object, place kind, and selector in the stop table.  Slot places also retain the class and effective slot identity.  Before storing, validate the index, hash-key presence, or unchanged slot definition so a stale reference cannot recreate a removed key or redirect a replaced slot.  Ordinary accessors perform representation and declared-type checks.  These checks do not make unsynchronized application mutations atomic.  Hash-table enumeration copies only the requested rows while holding the table's existing lock when synchronized; printers run after that lock is released.

## Debugger condition-handler scope: 2026-10-14

Review for catch and handler inspection found that SERVICE-COMMAND-LOOP runs with the stopped application's *ACTIVE-HANDLERS*.  BREAK enters the debugger directly, leaving an enclosing application HANDLER-CASE active.  Genera explicitly disables application handlers during debugger evaluation: [rebound variables](https://www.chai.uni-hamburg.de/~moeller/symbolics-info/documentation/Program-Development-Utilities.pdf#page=206), printed page 200.  The Common Lisp [handler selection rules](https://www.lispworks.com/documentation/HyperSpec/Body/09_ad.htm) explain the risk: an error in a debugger expression can invoke an outer application handler and leave the original stop.

Recommendation: reproduce this with an owned compiled target inside HANDLER-CASE, then evaluate ERROR in its retained frame and inspect the resulting job state.  If confirmed, bind the existing handler-cluster variable to NIL around the retained command loop.  This lets handlers established by debugger expressions work normally while protecting the paused program from command failures.  Original handlers must resume on nonlocal exit from the debugger, including application cleanup and continuation. ## Catch and handler record inspection: 2026-10-14

Reviewed Genera's [Show Catch Blocks and Show Condition Handlers](https://www.chai.uni-hamburg.de/~moeller/symbolics-info/documentation/Program-Development-Utilities.pdf#page=230), runtime/runtime.lisp, system/condition.lisp, and the existing frame-bound special-binding reader.  Mezzano's %CATCH establishes a stack-allocated two-element vector holding a tag and exit function through *ACTIVE-CATCH-HANDLERS*.  %HANDLER-BIND adds one cluster to *ACTIVE-HANDLERS*.  SIGNAL temporarily binds the remaining clusters while invoking a handler.  The Common Lisp [handler rules](https://www.lispworks.com/documentation/HyperSpec/Body/09_ad.htm) require every handler from the selected cluster to become inactive for that signaling process.

## Cold area buffers and file layout: 2026-10-14

The package-order correction passed source loading and cross compilation, then serialization exhausted the documented 2 GiB SBCL heap.  The failing operation was FINALIZE-AREAS calling ADJUST-ARRAY for a 142,606,336-byte octet buffer.  Live allocation was 1,793,410,192 bytes.  Source review found unconditional physical resizing during final padding, although area size and WRITE-SEQUENCE use the fill pointer.  Recommendation: retain capacity when sufficient, grow only when required, set the final logical length, and initialize the padding bytes.  Apply the same helper to the wired-function reservation and aligned areas.  Record actual capacities during the full build.  Tests must preserve every active byte, zero the padding, retain sufficient capacity, grow insufficient capacity, and write exactly the logical length.

Reviewed [FILL-POINTER](https://www.lispworks.com/documentation/HyperSpec/Body/f_fill_p.htm), [LENGTH](https://www.lispworks.com/documentation/HyperSpec/Body/f_length.htm), [WRITE-SEQUENCE](https://www.lispworks.com/documentation/HyperSpec/Body/f_wr_seq.htm), and [ADJUST-ARRAY](https://www.lispworks.com/documentation/HyperSpec/Body/f_adjust.htm).  Reading newly added array elements without initialization is undefined, so padding must be initialized explicitly.  The constructor and growth paths otherwise remain unchanged.  This is host serializer testing, which requires SBCL.

WRITE-AREAS also advances its disk cursor by the wired area's length for every saved area.  If another area is larger, the next write overlaps it.  Recommendation: advance by the area being written.  First reproduce the error with unequal synthetic area sizes, then check cumulative offsets, complete byte contents, and nonoverlapping mappings.  Repeat the clean image build at the same 2 GiB heap, then boot, inspect, collect, and restore it.  No guest format or virtual-address change is required.  Evidence: debugger-cold-build-package-order.log and tools/cold-generator2/write.lisp:120.

## Lexical-environment display research: 2026-10-14

Genera's Show Lexical Environment displays variables established by the selected frame's lexical ancestors, distinct from Show Local.  Source: [Program Development Utilities, printed page 225](https://www.chai.uni-hamburg.de/~moeller/symbolics-info/documentation/Program-Development-Utilities.pdf#page=231).  Mezzano's DEBUG-SOURCE-SCOPE in COMPILER/AST.LISP flattens visible bindings into identity-bearing records.  The runtime closure layout can include the current function's own captured cells as well as ancestor cells: LOWER-ENVIRONMENT pushes the current lambda before constructing its layout when that function allocates an environment.  Therefore selecting every environment-vector location would misclassify the function's own locals as inherited variables.

Before designing this command, test a nested function with an unused visible outer DEBUG 3 binding, a current local captured by another closure, and a shadowing ancestor binding.  Determine whether current preservation makes the unused outer binding accessible after its defining function returns.  Review source-owner identity through copying and inlining before adding metadata.  The existing four-field variable scope records and two-field binding descriptors have consumers that require their present layouts.  Keep these source findings separate from implemented command support.

The clean 8df36d81 build completed at the unchanged 2 GiB host heap limit.  Evidence: debugger-cold-build-generics.log.  Preserved its unbooted output as debugger-cold-generics-pristine-20261014.image, mode 0600.  Isolated first boot uses mezzano-debugger-generics-20261014.image on ports 4007/1236, PID 712038.  The acceptance drivers contain no constructor, FRAME-FUNCTION, allocator, or invalid-argument-helper refresh.  They compile owned fixtures only.  The separate interpreted-metadata fixture extension remains uncommitted and outside this image acceptance.

The owned native lexical observation confirmed the capture gap.  Its escaping DEBUG 3 closure's source scope contains ANCESTOR, ANCHOR, and CURRENT.  The runtime layout contains CURRENT in its own environment and ANCHOR in the parent environment, while ANCESTOR has no location.  ANCESTOR's defining activation has returned.  Explicit evaluation of LISPM-LEXICAL-OBSERVATION::ANCESTOR entered the expected :UNAVAILABLE-BINDING child, and typed Abort, parent continuation, values 42/43, and owned release passed.  Evidence: debugger-lexical-environment-observe.log and debugger-lexical-ancestor-rejection.log.  The scope records preserve the binding identity, but program free-variable capture omits the unused outer binding.  Correcting capture through the compiler's existing analyses remains required.  The product reference now states this limit while the compiler-preservation plan remains unchecked.

Additional source review found a capture-lifetime constraint.  CONVERT-DYNAMIC-EXTENT runs first in the optimizer, before LOWER-ENVIRONMENT computes closure capture.  Its AST-LET method converts declared dynamic-extent list/vector initializers without considering debugger-only capture.  Adding unused ancestor bindings only in lower-environment would therefore allow an escaping debug environment to retain a stack-allocated object after its defining activation returns.  The preservation design must resolve that lifetime before dynamic-extent lowering.  No capture implementation or representation change has been made.

## Coalesced disk page-in: 2026-10-14

The pager reads one 4-KiB page per synchronous disk request and performs one cross-CPU TLB rendezvous per page.  The measured ATA request costs explain why a collection that must read hundreds of MiB after restoration can exceed the HTTP deadline.  The established cause of the reproduced timeout is the 18.99-second major pause.  The contribution and improvement of page-in coalescing still require measurement.

Recommendation: coalesce a demand read with following pages into one read of at most 64 KiB.  Include only present block-map entries with consecutive real backing blocks, no zero-fill, no already resident PTE, and a count within the disk's maximum transfer.  Select a power-of-two count to match the buddy allocator.  If that contiguous frame allocation cannot be satisfied, use the existing single-page allocation and reclamation path.  Zero-fill and resident/COW handling retain their existing paths.  Perform the disk read before installing the pages.  Initialize each frame's active type, virtual address, block identity, and replacement-list links.  Retain each page's writable and tracking flags.  Use one existing TLB rendezvous for the installed range, with a local invalidation for each page.  No new library, transport, timeout, global configuration, or eager image preload is needed.

Review evidence: SUPERVISOR/PAGER.LISP holds the VM write lock around the slow fault path.  SUPERVISOR/PHYSICAL.LISP allocates and releases buddy blocks at power-of-two orders and marks only their head, so page-in must mark every frame before treating them as independently replaceable pages.  X86-64 TLB-SHOOTDOWN-RANGE participates in the existing rendezvous and remote full flush.  ARM64 FLUSH-TLB-SINGLE already invalidates across cores.  The existing ATA path supports the aligned 64-KiB DMA request used in the read-only experiment.  Read-only and committed backing blocks can be prefetched without changing their reservation accounting.

Required tests:

- [x] Candidate counts, transfer limit, discontinuous blocks, absent/zero/lazy entries, already resident pages, and non-power-of-two runs.
- [x] Frame identities, flags, replacement links, contents, and independent release after a real coalesced read.
- [x] Single-page behavior under insufficient contiguous free frames and zero-fill behavior.
- [x] Reservation accounting and full GC on x86-64.
- [x] Normal and parked snapshot tests on x86-64.
- [x] Saved-baseline Chromium replay with the same 15-second deadline and collector timing.
- [x] Clean build, boot, and normal/parked restoration before final image acceptance.

ARM64 source compatibility will be reviewed.  ARM64 execution remains untested.  Disk errors must follow the existing explicit pager failure path rather than install partial data.

Further review narrows coalescing to existing page-table entries.  The first demanded entry already exists, and prefetch stops before an absent page-table level.  Mapping the selected run then needs no additional page-table allocation after acquiring its frames.  The ordinary next fault creates a missing table through the existing path.  This avoids a new allocation failure inside range installation.

The internal run-count helper takes the disk-derived maximum page count as an argument.  Its caller supplies that limit. ## Older compiled lexical environments: 2026-10-15

Source review found a compatibility case for the new compiler-only owner slot.  FULL-EVAL's lexical-environment MAKE-LOAD-FORM delegates to MAKE-LOAD-FORM-SAVING-SLOTS.  SYSTEM/FILE-COMPILER.LISP allocates the class without initialization and writes only the slots present and bound when saved.  ALLOCATE-INSTANCE in SYSTEM/CLOS/CLOSETTE.LISP does not apply initforms.  A compiled file saved before %SOURCE-OWNER existed can therefore load an environment whose new slot is unbound.  The current direct readers in environment extension/copying and ancestry conversion would then signal instead of reporting missing ownership.  This is source evidence, pending native reproduction.  It is distinct from runtime scope plists whose ancestry key is absent.

Recommendation: define one compiler environment-owner reader that returns :UNKNOWN when this optional metadata slot is unbound, and use it in extension, copying, and ancestry conversion.  Preserve ordinary slot access errors for the existing environment fields.  Add a native compiled-file fixture with the owner slot omitted from its load form, the same omission an older file produces.  Reproduce the current failure, then require extension/copying and ancestry conversion to preserve unavailable ownership after loading and full GC.  Existing known-owner and binding-identity tests must still pass.  No change to general CLOS allocation or load-form semantics is indicated.  Complete the running clean d3f5ca53 native suites before changing production code or their fixture sources.

## Recurrent SWANK startup wait: 2026-10-15

The isolated mode browser suite failed before its fixture and before retained OPEN-SESSION submission.  Diagnostic request 2668 connected in 0.489 ms and sent the 78-byte SWANK-REQUIRE request by 08:33:07.013410 UTC.  Its first recv(6) received zero bytes and timed out at 08:33:22.028572 UTC after 15.015080 seconds.  Session-lock wait was 22 microseconds.  Fresh cleanup request 2669 completed initial REQUIRE in 4.990 ms and returned :expired-session from STOPS in 4.471 ms.  No mode fixture job/stop/session was created, and cleanup is not reported as a successful release.  Evidence: /tmp/web-standard-values-startup-phase.json and captured isolated server log.  The serial event history contains a completed require worker, encode-message, a large indentation update, and CONNECTION-RESET without timestamps.  It cannot locate the delay or identify causation.

Recommendation: stop publication and further browser retries, preserve the exact logs/ledger, inspect the pure initial REQUIRE/control-thread/TCP paths and current process state, then capture packet chronology during controlled reproduction.  tcpdump, dumpcap, and tcpflow are absent.  Install tcpdump on the authorized development host for this diagnostic capture.  Add no project dependency and change no retry/deadline behavior.  Existing permission to install host tools applies.  The Web agent separately reviews host transport read/deadline/close handling without edits or traffic.  Stable native standard-value loading has not occurred, and its seven-record baseline remains retained.

Twenty controlled fresh initial-REQUIRE connections completed in 5.0–6.5 ms with no half-second observation trigger.  Read-only native state reported zero retained jobs/stops and the module already loaded.  This does not explain the failed connection.  Evidence: debugger-swank-startup-reproduction.json and the narrow loopback packet capture.  Recommendation: install a temporary observer through SWANK's existing *EVENT-HOOK* on isolated 4007.  Retain timestamps and connection/thread identity for request dispatch, return dispatch, and indentation-update dispatch without changing reply handling.  Run another bounded pure-REQUIRE reproduction with mailbox samples on slow replies, then remove the hook and its owned data.  Match the stage records to packet times before drawing a cause.  No stable source or retry/deadline change is authorized by these observations.

The timestamped 100-connection reproduction completed without a 15-second timeout.  Connection 72 was initially reported as taking 2.598960 seconds.  That elapsed value includes monitor overhead, as diagnosed below.  Its initial-REQUIRE dispatch and return both occurred at guest time 4001042575630000, after the delay.  The half-second sample itself waited through collection and observed the new control thread on Garbage Collector Cvar.  The collector was waiting for RELEASE-MEMORY-RANGE-IN-PAGER.  Mailbox samples showed no queued reply stranded on a sleeping control thread.  These observations identify a GC-related wait for that sampled connection, not the cause of the earlier 15-second failure.  The first 180-second capture ended before the observed loop completed, so do not claim it captures that slow connection. Source review confirms an independent host concurrency limitation.  file-server/server.lisp accepts one socket, runs HANDLE-CLIENT until disconnect or its 60-second idle timeout, then accepts another.  Each guest retains its remote-filesystem connection.  SWANK startup opens HOME/.slime-secret before registration.  A second guest's authentication probe can therefore wait behind the first guest's connection.  The installation guide documents this restriction.  This establishes a possible blocking path, not causation for the earlier timeout.

Recommendation: give each accepted SBCL-host connection one Lisp worker while the accept thread continues.  Reuse HANDLE-CLIENT's per-client *CLIENT*, fresh eight-entry *FILE-TABLE*, stream positions, and protocol buffers.  The command table is read-only during service.  Keep the public RUN-FILE-SERVER, SPAWN-FILE-SERVER, and KILL-SERVER behavior.  Track accepted workers so shutdown closes their sockets and waits for cleanup.  Each worker must close its file handles and socket through UNWIND-PROTECT.  Protect ownership transfer against thread-creation failure and asynchronous server shutdown.  Propagate unexpected worker or cleanup failures to the server owner.  Treat EOF and configured idle expiration as connection termination, while preserving command error replies.  Remove HANDLE-CLIENT's blanket IGNORE-ERRORS.  Prefer the existing threading facilities and add no library.  This bounded increment targets the SBCL backend.  Preserve the existing non-SBCL backend's behavior and identify its concurrency limit in documentation.

Worker-ownership refinement: keep the active-client list private to RUN-FILE-SERVER's owner thread.  Workers do not mutate that list.  The owner adds accepted sockets/workers under SBCL interruption scopes, reaps completed workers through join, and propagates unexpected returned conditions.  A worker wakes the owner after cleanup through the existing thread-interruption facility.  Shutdown cancels socket I/O and joins every remaining worker.  This avoids a shared registry mutex and adds no library or ASDF dependency.  Test creation/publication/shutdown races before accepting the implementation.

Descriptor ownership refinement: SBCL socket shutdown reads the descriptor while socket close closes it before invalidating the stored descriptor.  Concurrent shutdown and close can therefore act on a reused descriptor.  Use one server-local mutex around stream creation, socket shutdown, and socket close.  Keep request processing outside that mutex.  Mark shutdown under the same mutex so a worker that starts late skips stream creation.  Test shutdown during worker startup and verify that unrelated descriptors remain open.

SOCKET-CLOSE closes a cached socket stream.  WAIT-UNTIL-FD-USABLE accepts SERVE-EVENTS NIL, which limits this wait to the listener descriptor.  EAGAIN and EINTR map to INTERRUPTED-ERROR. ## Selected-frame special variables: 2026-10-15

Genera's Program Development Utilities, printed pages 200–201, says lexical evaluation uses the current selected frame's variable bindings, while dynamic evaluation uses the point of error.  Printed page 226 specifies Show Special SYMBOL with :Environment Program/Debugger/Streams.  Omitted environment follows the current frame environment, and a mentioned environment defaults to Program.  Source: https://www.chai.uni-hamburg.de/~moeller/symbolics-info/documentation/Program-Development-Utilities.pdf#page=232 .  Current Mezzano evaluation still uses the stopped thread's innermost special bindings except for its debugger-owned histories and four controls.  This remaining difference is documented.

Source inspection: SERVICE-FRAME-BINDING-CELLS already identifies established x86-64 binding cells between saved frame boundaries and traverses the existing special-stack chain.  Runtime SYMBOL-VALUE, BOUNDP, MAKUNBOUND, and setters share SYMBOL-VALUE-CELL lookup, with a separate global-cell fallback.  Copying a selected binding's value into PROGV and copying it back would change identity and delay writes to the program's cell.  That would not establish correct access through called functions or nested debugging.  Review the existing resolver and compiler fast lookup together before recommending evaluation changes.  A read-only selected-frame lookup can first be tested against nested bindings, repeated bindings, unbound cells, and global fallback without claiming evaluation support.  Stable standard-value publication remains the current increment.  No selected-frame special-variable implementation change has been made.

Compiled x86-64 special-variable reads use a per-thread cache keyed by the global value cell.  On a miss they call %SYMBOL-VALUE-CELL-BY-CELL.  Binding installs the new cell in that cache, and unbinding invalidates a matching cached cell.  A selected-frame lookup added only to the interpreter would therefore leave called compiled code reading a younger binding.  Any evaluation design must preserve cell identity across both paths and respect bindings established during evaluation.  No runtime/cache change is recommended before the read-only selected-frame tests.  References: compiler/backend/x86-64/misc.lisp:40, compiler/backend/x86-64/codegen.lisp:1112, runtime/symbol.lisp:172.

Continuation review changes the read-only test scope.  CALL-WITH-PROMPT allocates a separate stack and retains the previous stack object in its special-stack prompt record.  Physical addresses from successive segments need not be ordered.  A selected-frame lookup based only on cell-address greater than frame pointer would therefore be insufficient.  First observe binding ownership across a real CALL-WITH-PROMPT stop and compare it with the existing per-frame range inspection.  Include repeated bindings and an outer binding across the stack transition.  Use a private native fixture on isolated 4007 while the Web agent tests stable 4006.  Do not change runtime lookup, the compiler cache, or stable service.  References: system/delimited-continuations.lisp:35, system/delimited-continuations-x86-64.lisp:3, system/debug.lisp:650, and system/debugger-service.lisp:606.

The first native CALL-WITH-PROMPT observation compiled without warnings/failure and completed with owned cleanup.  Values 33 and 22 occupy the new stack near address 35813501960000, while outer value 11 occupies the older stack near 35813497829104.  Existing per-frame inspection assigned both younger cells only to INNER and the older cell only to OUTER.  Thus the existing ownership test passed in this topology.  An address-greater-than-selected-FP lookup would still choose a younger binding when OUTER is selected.  Evidence: debugger-selected-special-observe.log, ending :CONTINUATION-BINDING-OBSERVATION-FINISHED.  No production code changed.

Return the original matching cell, global fallback, or explicit unavailable status for an unsupported frame.  Test ordinary and prompt stacks, repeated bindings, bound NIL, unbound cells, global fallback, exact cell identity, and full GC before considering a production helper.  This changes no evaluation lookup, compiler cache, stream binding, or stable service.
