## Show Special command design and implementation

Genera's Program Development Utilities, printed page 226, specifies :Show Special SYMBOL with :Environment Program, Debugger, or Streams.  The omitted default follows the current frame's environment, and the mentioned default is Program.  Source: https://www.chai.uni-hamburg.de/~moeller/symbolics-info/documentation/Program-Development-Utilities.pdf#page=232 .  The approved catch-block command already implements its documented Boolean defaults, destination display, and preserved frame/history behavior.  This increment continues the authorized environment-inspection work.

Recommendation: add one retained string-result operation, :SPECIAL, accepting (symbol-source environment), where symbol-source is a copied string and environment is :PROGRAM or :DEBUGGER.  The Command Processor preserves symbol source for reading by the stopped thread under its validated *PACKAGE* and with *READ-EVAL* NIL.  Read exactly one symbol during execution.  Reader errors, extra forms, and non-symbol objects use the existing child-debugger boundary.  Replay compares copied arguments with EQUAL and returns the original result.  The browser sends source text and an explicitly validated environment selector.  No protocol symbol extension, stop field, dependency, or evaluation change is required.

Program reads the original cell returned by SERVICE-FRAME-SPECIAL-CELL for the selected frame.  Preserve the distinction between bound NIL, unbound, and unavailable.  Debugger reads the nine retained history values for their nine symbols and current debugger-command bindings for other symbols, including the four validated controls.  The temporary - binding follows its existing dynamic lifetime and gains no retained slot.  Both omitted and mentioned :Environment select Program for the retained program frames currently exposed.  This default is independent of lexical/dynamic evaluation mode.  Recognize Streams in command assistance but reject its unsupported environment before accepting a command ID.  State the environment and Program frame in the result.  Preserve selection, evaluation mode, histories, and program cells.

Tests: native selected-frame values across prompt segments and full GC, NIL/unbound/missing cells, retained history and ephemeral -, debugger controls/package resolution, argument copying and replay, malformed input and printer child Abort/recovery, no command-ID consumption on unsupported options, continuation, and owned cleanup.  Chromium must exercise typed command completion, the required-symbol menu prompt, environment choices, frame differences, reload/lost replies, nested printer recovery, unsupported Streams, and subsequent Listener evaluation.  Test only isolated 4007/8766 until those pass.  Read and update product/API/test documentation, review source, commit, and push.  ARM64 and restoration remain separate untested cases.

## Historical special-variable evaluation: source review

Genera's Program Development Utilities, printed pages 200–201, states that lexical evaluation uses the selected frame's variable bindings, while dynamic evaluation uses the bindings at the point of error.  The existing read-only helper now finds selected live cells.  Changing only the interpreter's symbol access would leave compiled callees using a different environment.  runtime/symbol.lisp resolves cells through %SYMBOL-VALUE-CELL-BY-CELL.  The x86-64 compiler's FAST-SYMBOL-VALUE-CELL caches original cells in 128 per-thread entries, and binding/unbinding instructions update or invalidate those entries.  ARM64 has a corresponding cache in runtime/runtime-arm64.lisp.  The real special stack also contains unwind and continuation records and must retain its control-flow meaning.

Recommendation for the next investigation: prototype a dynamically scoped lookup boundary in the existing cell resolver, retaining the physical special/unwind chain and original value cells.  Determine whether the existing special-binding representation can carry this boundary without adding a thread slot.  Reads and writes from both interpreted and compiled code must agree.  New LET/PROGV bindings must shadow it normally.  Entry and exit must invalidate cached cells coherently, including asynchronous interruption and nonlocal exit.  Inspect existing foothold scopes before choosing that implementation.  Rebinding copies and copying values back would change cell identity and defer writes, so they cannot satisfy the required behavior.  No runtime change has been made for this investigation.

Required evidence before production integration: immediate writes visible through existing compiled closures, bound NIL/unbound/global fallback, selected outer versus inner cells, new dynamic bindings and unbinding, cache collisions/hits/misses, nested contexts and debugger children, cleanup on THROW/Abort/printer errors, asynchronous interruption, continuation-stack boundaries, full GC, parked/executing restoration, and ordinary-runtime behavior without a lookup boundary.  Keep reader/printer controls, retained histories, streams, and application-handler suppression explicit.  Proceed with the current command's Web acceptance and stable deployment before executing this runtime experiment.

### Debugger command I/O prerequisite: 2026-10-15

Web source review found that fresh Listener evaluations default to batch input.  A batch worker binds QUERY-IO to its fixed input string and reaches EOF.  SERVICE-DEBUGGER and RUN-SERVICE-COMMAND inherit that application stream.  A stop in a thread without a retained evaluation also has no remote input/output route.  Existing restart readers and Modify share this limitation.  The [Common Lisp stream reference](https://www.lispworks.com/documentation/HyperSpec/Body/v_debug_.htm) specifies QUERY-IO for questions and DEBUG-IO for interactive debugging.  Genera's printed page 229 describes Return prompting.  Enabling only interactive jobs or navigating to a Listener leaves the same guest-side ownership problem.

Recommendation: give each accepted debugger command its own retained two-way stream, using the existing EVALUATION-INPUT-STREAM and EVALUATION-OUTPUT-STREAM classes unchanged.  Source review confirms that those streams own their buffers, positions, EOF state, wait counts, and event.  They have no evaluation-job backpointer.  Add one IO slot to SERVICE-COMMAND.  Bind the seven standard streams around command execution, close both component streams on command completion/unwind/cancellation, and retain their data with the existing command record until stop release.  Each new command starts with fresh input.  A recursive debugger uses its own command streams, preserving the parent's suspended reader.  Application cleanup runs after these debugger stream bindings unwind.

Extend DEBUGGER-COMMAND-RESULT with input length/EOF/wait state and output length.  Add DEBUGGER-COMMAND-OUTPUT(handle,id,start,end) and SUPPLY-DEBUGGER-COMMAND-INPUT(lease,id,offset,text,:eof).  Output reads copy retained characters.  Input uses the existing offset/content replay rules and the controller's lease.  Fresh current-boot handles can supply input to a restored running command without resubmitting it.  A prior-boot command still rejects command replay.  Historical commands created before this addition have no I/O context and retain their results.  No new session, worker, job, registry, dependency, or EOF-reset operation is required.

Native I/O tests must cover a batch evaluation and a jobless thread, all stream bindings and restoration, two reads in one command, EOF followed by fresh command input, recursive reader Abort, exact input replay/conflicts, lost replies, lease ownership, close/release, and snapshot restoration.  Existing interactive-command tests must use the new command channel.  Browser work must render the same command output/input in Listener and standalone Debugger, preserve input drafts by stop/command identity, and follow a cleanup's new root stop through guest ownership. GDB's bounded saved-frame walk shows repeated TYPEP → lazy interpreter invocation → EVAL-LAMBDA → NAMESTRING → PATHNAME → ERROR cycles. Remove IGNORE-ERRORS there.  A valid present pathname supplies its namestring, and an invalid present value must propagate its error. Install the corrected EVAL-LAMBDA from its checked-in form, compile/load its full file, and repeat the runtime/TYPEP source and structure tests. ### Navigation after a closed stop: 2026-10-15

Review found that a Return cleanup can enter a new root stop after the original stop closes.  Listener ownership already follows its evaluation's active stop.  Standalone navigation retains the closed original record and offers only parent/child links.  A jobless cleanup root has neither link.  Display thread names are non-unique and provide no ownership relation.

Recommendation: add :THREAD-STOP to stop information for a closed record.  Under the existing service lock, use SERVICE-THREAD-CURRENT-STOP with that record's retained thread object and return a fresh handle for its current leaf stop.  Active records and threads without an active stop return NIL.  Encode the handle in both direct information and monitor-state through existing token helpers.  The Web agent will expose Current Stop only on a closed record with a non-NIL link, using existing selection controls.  This preserves the closed command's retained output and avoids a new slot, registry, selection state, or name-based inference.

Native tests must verify the link during Return cleanup and NIL after continuation.  Protocol tests must verify direct/monitor token encoding, active-record NIL, and link removal after cleanup.  Browser acceptance must exercise a jobless cleanup root with duplicate display thread names.  This is the next bounded increment before browser Return acceptance.  The native Return commit is 9e0cbc4c, and its API documentation commit is Slime f57b572a.

Reviewed Genera Reinvoke (Program Development Utilities, printed page 229), the existing frame-return boundary and epilogue, the x86-64 ABI, APPLY, DEFINE-LAP-FUNCTION, backend argument setup, and argument lowering.  The ABI permits callees to modify incoming stack arguments, so those slots cannot establish an original-argument snapshot.  The backend receives callable/count/required/optional/rest values, while keyword and special-argument lowering changes their compiler bindings.  Current/original argument metadata and callable recovery require further design.  No argument-reconstruction claim is made here.

Recommendation: first test a private Reinvoke transfer with an explicit function designator and finite argument list.  Reuse FRAME-RETURN-CONTEXT and %%UNWIND-TO.  After cleanup, a small Lisp LAP adapter adopts the selected activation's frame pointer and stack position, retaining its original caller link and return address.  Allocate three rooted slots and alignment padding in that frame, APPLY the replacement with the new arguments, then LEAVE/RET with its multiple values.  Incoming-argument GC metadata preserves the four helper arguments through the physical transition.  Retain the detached younger stack through that transition.  This uses an ordinary call after unwinding and permits new arities while the original caller removes its original stack arguments.  Evaluating the replacement before unwinding would use the wrong dynamic bindings and cleanup order.

Compiler warning diagnosis: COMPILE-FILE ends with literal (VALUES (TRUENAME OUTPUT-STREAM) NIL NIL), independently of detected conditions.  COMPILE receives the unspecified secondary/tertiary values of COMPILE-LAMBDA, which returns its function object.  WITH-COMPILATION-UNIT currently establishes only a Boolean binding and records no diagnostics.  Parallel file workers handle errors for the existing return FIFO but have no warning bookkeeping.  The [COMPILE-FILE specification](https://www.lispworks.com/documentation/HyperSpec/Body/f_cmp_fi.htm) requires a true warning flag for WARNING or ERROR, and a true failure flag for ERROR or WARNING excluding STYLE-WARNING.  This confirms a compiler result-reporting defect.

### Current parameter identity metadata: 2026-10-15

Reviewed source lambda translation, AST copying, argument/key/environment/special lowering, binding preservation, existing frame-local and special-cell readers, and [Genera Reinvoke, printed page 229](https://www.chai.uni-hamburg.de/~moeller/symbolics-info/documentation/Program-Development-Utilities.pdf#page=235). Original entry snapshots establish supplied arguments, but source parameter bindings disappear from the lowered lambda-list slots.  Parameter names alone cannot distinguish a source binding from an inner binding with the same name.

Recommendation: retain a DEBUG 3 source-parameter layout in LAMBDA-INFORMATION before lowering.  Keep references to existing binding objects, remap them through COPY-FORM after the body has established all replacements, and encode existing lexical binding descriptors at code generation.  Encode special parameters by their symbol.  Append function debug-info field 13: #(:PARAMETERS required optional rest keys enable-keys allow-other-keys).  Required entries are descriptors, optional entries are (binding supplied-binding), and key entries are (keyword binding supplied-binding).  A missing supplied variable remains NIL.  Special descriptors are #(:SPECIAL symbol).  The layout contains no initializer forms or source AST objects after emission.  Lower policies and generated cleanup functions have no record. Add an internal service reader returning the layout, (descriptor value available) entries, and a record-level unavailability reason.  Validate the live eligible owning frame first.  Read lexical values by descriptor identity through existing frame-local storage.  Reuse SERVICE-FRAME-BINDING-CELLS for special parameters, selecting the oldest matching binding within that activation's interval, so inner LET rebindings cannot replace the parameter cell.  An absent or unbound parameter cell reports unavailable.  Do not substitute the thread's innermost binding, global value, or original argument.  Preserve NIL as an available value.  Invalid metadata and storage errors propagate.

### Reinvoke global definition provenance: 2026-10-15

Reviewed DEFUN, COMPILE, lambda-name parsing, native/cross DEFUN expansion, function references, macro installation, and tracing.  A symbol-shaped display name does not identify a global definition.  TRACE creates an entry closure with (LAMBDA-NAME TRACE-WRAPPER), while the global TRACE-WRAPPER function has a different argument list.  Inferring global identity from that label would select the wrong callable.  This is a design finding before implementing resolution.  FDEFINITION also hides active trace wrappers, and %COERCE-TO-CALLABLE postpones an undefined symbol's error until invocation.

Recommendation: extend the existing internal declaration to (LAMBDA-NAME name :GLOBAL T).  DEFUN and the cross-compiler's DEFUN expansion emit that flag.  COMPILE adds it only when compiling source for a nonmacro name.  Already compiled functions retain their source provenance when installed under an alias.  Pass1 retains #(:GLOBAL-FUNCTION name) in the lambda plist, and the backend appends that record as debug-info field 14 at DEBUG 3.  Display-only names and older functions have no provenance record.  The existing AST plist copy preserves this immutable record.  No reverse registry, new dependency, call ABI, or global binding mutation is needed.

Add an internal callable resolver: without provenance, return the exact executing callable.  With provenance, validate the name, reject a current macro or absent definition through UNDEFINED-FUNCTION before unwinding, and read FUNCTION-REFERENCE-FUNCTION without creating a missing reference.  This preserves active trace wrappers and uses the current global definition.  Return the provenance record as a second value.  A later retained command will resolve again after confirmation immediately before unwinding.

Tests: ordinary DEFUN and named COMPILE source, a global closure, SETF/CAS names, definition replacement, active tracing and replacement while traced, unbound/macro replacement before cleanup, local/anonymous callable identity, the trace entry closure's display-name collision, unchanged compiled-function provenance under alias installation, full GC, compiled-file loading, and both target emitters.  Repeat compiler diagnostic/publication and internal Reinvoke tests affected by COMPILE/DEBUG changes.  Use native x86-64 4008 with normal LOAD.  Cross-source review does not establish a cross build.  Public commands, argument reconstruction, saved activation restoration, and safe transfer of stack-allocated argument objects remain separate work.

Source inspection also leaves a lifetime question for the public transfer: REINVOKE-FRAME copies an argument-list spine but preserves its contained objects.  An argument changed to an object allocated inside the selected activation can have shorter storage lifetime than replacement execution.  Existing tests establish heap argument identity and a DX list spine, not arbitrary DX payloads.  Review and test that lifetime before claiming public support for such payloads.

Provenance review kept PARSE-LAMBDA's existing return values: PASS1 reads :GLOBAL from the declaration list it already receives.  The first uncompiled parser edit had an unmatched parenthesis, caught by the form scanner before publication.  The simplified implementation leaves that parser unchanged.  Named COMPILE wraps only a well-formed lambda prefix; invalid heads and missing lambda lists retain their existing compiler errors instead of becoming valid source through annotation.

Further provenance review requires distinguishing an explicit local/anonymous callable from an older function with missing metadata.  NIL cannot represent both cases without silently retaining an obsolete global definition.  Recommendation before final publication: field 14 is #(:GLOBAL-FUNCTION name) for a known global definition, :EXACT-CALLABLE for known local/anonymous code, and NIL for unavailable provenance.  The resolver returns function, provenance, and unavailability reason.  Missing metadata returns NIL/NIL/:UNAVAILABLE-CALLABLE-PROVENANCE.  Display-only names use the explicit exact marker.  Extend the native suite with a retained pre-marker function and marker checks for local/tracing/macro-source code.  This supersedes the initial NIL-as-exact fallback.  The first native publication is still running with that initial implementation; preserve its result and then test the refined representation before committing.

### Remote filesystem failure during provenance publication: 2026-10-15

The first provenance driver loaded only BACKEND.LISP, then stopped while closing COMPILE-FILE's PASS1.LLF output, before PASS1 LOAD or later modules/tests.  The output path is compiler/pass1.llf.  No provenance suite passed.  Evidence: debugger-reinvoke-global-native.log and its retained job state.  Two normal reconnect inspections stopped waiting in SWANK initialization; neither reached debugger commands.

Read-only QEMU GDB inspection resolved the owning evaluation through the current image map's (DEFGLOBAL *ALL-THREADS*) source-location record.  It found the retained condition END-OF-FILE with a TCP-STREAM, in READ-PRESERVING-WHITESPACE inside remote COMMAND/FLUSH-BUFFER/CLOSE during COMPILE-FILE cleanup.  The evaluation remains in SERVICE-COMMAND-LOOP while holding REMOTE-FILE-HOST's mutex.  SWANK 4005 is waiting for that mutex in OPEN-USING-HOST, called by SLIME-SECRET/AUTHENTICATE-CLIENT.  Thus new debugger connections cannot authenticate until the filesystem critical section exits.  GDB detached after every sample.  Earlier diagnostic scripts used another image's obsolete root address and then failed decoding a name/finishing the walk.  Those failed samples are retained and do not establish additional thread facts.  Exact condition decoding and the Swank wait stack succeeded.

The host file server has a 60-second idle deadline.  The guest remote client also passes a 60-second TCP idle timeout.  The partial PASS1 output contains 524,288 bytes, last written at 12:56:11.229616 CDT.  The host driver reported the stop at 12:57:13.386968 CDT, 62.16 seconds later, after COMPILE-FILE reported 79.89 seconds.  Host protocol logging ended with WRITE/CLOSE.  These facts implicate idle connection expiry, but do not distinguish which endpoint closed first.  Preserve both configured timers until a targeted test establishes the necessary change.

Source review: remote streams keep local buffers and reopen server file handles for each transaction.  CALL-WITH-CONNECTION's empty-read tickle checks TCP errors but does not establish bidirectional availability at orderly peer EOF.  A request/response filesystem transaction needs an established connection.  WITH-MUTEX already supports resignal outside the lock, but this client selects FILE-ERROR only, excluding END-OF-FILE.  Its explicit RETRY restart lives inside that lock.  The generic error handler closes the cached connection before clearing its slot, allowing a close error to reenter that handler.  Review the minimal correction against the existing EOF/one-retry/no-CREATE-replay tests before editing.  Required acceptance includes full-duplex cache eligibility, unchanged mutation replay limits, original condition identity outside the host lock, RETRY availability, and concurrent authentication while a filesystem operation is stopped.

Native 4008 is isolated.  Original/stable/browser VMs and the stable Web service remain unchanged.  Preserve the failed state and partial LLF before any recovery.  A restart can recover this isolated test world after the source correction is ready, but does not constitute fixing the failure.  Repeat the failed publication and a direct failure/control-access test after the correction.

Recommendation after reading both endpoints: keep the existing sixty-second idle timers.  Remote-file streams open transient server handles for each buffered transaction, so an idle cached transport may expire without invalidating the Lisp stream.  Reuse that transport only while its TCP connection is ESTABLISHED with no pending error.  Abort and clear other cached states before sending a new transaction.  TCP CLOSE-WAIT remains valid for general TCP half-close behavior, but cannot serve a fresh request/response filesystem transaction.  No request replay is added after mutation begins.

Move the existing RETRY restart outside the host mutex and snapshot scope, with a reconnect flag consumed under the mutex on the next attempt.  Use WITH-MUTEX's existing :RESIGNAL-ERRORS T so END-OF-FILE and other errors reach the debugger after releasing the lock.  Preserve the original condition object.  Clear the cached slot before abort-close.  If abort-close also fails, signal a SIMPLE-ERROR retaining both original condition objects in FORMAT-ARGUMENTS.  Keep semantic server SIMPLE-FILE-ERROR replies from invalidating a synchronized connection.  Preserve the existing single automatic TCP-error retry and the OPEN preflight's single safe PROBE retry.  A stale transport discarded before a transaction does not consume that PROBE retry.

Extend TEST-REMOTE-EOF with a stale CLOSE-WAIT cached connection before a mutation transaction, errors observed outside the host mutex, explicit RETRY from outside the lock, exact primary/cleanup condition objects, and deterministic peer failure during a real operation.  Update the repeated-PROBE fixture to provide two responding peer connections: cache validation now treats orderly half-close like an already CLOSED connection, so one safe PROBE retry means two sent PROBEs.  CREATE remains unreplayed.  Test new SWANK authentication while an owned filesystem failure is stopped.  Host server source/deployment will remain unchanged unless these tests reveal another defect.

Preserve the currently stopped 4008 VM as failure evidence.  Prefer a fresh isolated native working copy on a different free loopback port for acceptance, after verifying resources and protected process arguments.  Use the preserved read-only Return-confirmation checkpoint, finish its owned restoration fixture, and publish the filesystem correction before recompiling the tested compiler increments.  This keeps the failed world available for inspection rather than overwriting it.

### Reinvoke current argument reconstruction: 2026-10-15

Reviewed the existing entry snapshot, source parameter layout/reader, callable resolver, internal transfer, and the delegated manual/UI review.  [Genera Reinvoke, printed page 229](https://www.chai.uni-hamburg.de/~moeller/symbolics-info/documentation/Program-Development-Utilities.pdf#page=235) defaults to current arguments and permits new arguments.  Its description does not define every Common Lisp optional/rest/key mutation combination.  The following policy is Mezzano's.  [Optional parameters](https://www.lispworks.com/documentation/HyperSpec/Body/03_dab.htm), [rest parameters](https://www.lispworks.com/documentation/HyperSpec/Body/03_dac.htm), and [keyword parameters](https://www.lispworks.com/documentation/HyperSpec/Body/03_dad.htm) determine the new ordinary call.

Recommendation: add one internal argument-construction helper in DEBUGGER-SERVICE taking the existing source layout, descriptor/value/availability observations, and original supplied sequence.  Supply every current required and optional value explicitly.  Copy the current source rest spine when present.  With &KEY and no source rest parameter, copy the original tail after required/optional positions.  Overlay each declared keyword's leftmost value with its current parameter value.  Prepend absent declared keys in declaration order.  Preserve unknown pairs and later duplicate pairs.  The helper never mutates the source rest or original snapshot spine and preserves referenced objects.

Every declared optional/key value becomes supplied, so defaults do not execute and supplied-p variables are recomputed by ordinary argument binding.  Edited supplied-p variables are not constructor inputs.  In combined rest/key cases, current named key bindings take precedence over conflicting rest entries.  Original mode will use the existing original snapshot instead, retaining omissions and rerunning applicable defaults in the chosen callee.  Neither mode rolls back mutations to referenced objects.  Preserve :ALLOW-OTHER-KEYS pairs and its ordinary declared-key role.  Do not add acceptance flags or discard unknown pairs to make a different definition accept them.

Reject unavailable required/optional/rest/key values, improper or circular tails, odd keyword tails, nonsymbol keyword names, and a final count at CALL-ARGUMENTS-LIMIT before transfer.  Multiple declarations of one keyword must have EQL current values.  Otherwise one ordinary keyword pair cannot represent their values.  Use the first such value when they are EQL.  Mezzano's x86-64 and ARM64 EQL implementations compare double/short floats by representation, distinguishing signed zeros, and use ordinary numeric equality for other boxed numeric types.  This preserves object identity for nonnumeric objects while accepting equal numeric values under the language's EQL rule.

The native increment will test pure construction and live parameter readers, default/supplied-p consequences, required/optional writes, rest/key disagreements, missing and repeated keys, unknown and :ALLOW-OTHER-KEYS pairs, nonkeyword symbol names, duplicate declared keys, zero and 499 arguments, invalid/unavailable cases before cleanup, source spine identity, heap payload identity, closures/specials, GC and prompts.  The public operation, confirmation, browser tests, saved activation restoration, and stack-allocated payload lifetime remain separate acceptance.  No compiler representation change or dependency is required.

For the later retained command, capture the current callable and constructed argument spine once before preview and confirmation.  Replaying accepted input must use that candidate.  A concurrent redefinition after preparation does not replace the displayed candidate.  This supersedes the initial proposal to resolve again after confirmation.  Print every argument by index with bounded per-value printing, since SERVICE-PRINT truncates a whole list after twenty elements.  The existing command I/O, expression reader, nested Abort, history, and replay mechanisms suffice.

The internal constructor will return arguments, reason, and the unavailable binding descriptor.  A successful zero-argument candidate is NIL with no reason.  This follows the existing metadata readers' availability convention and lets a later command identify the missing parameter before prompting or unwinding.  Malformed lists/metadata and conflicting duplicate-key values signal errors.

Fixture review before native compilation caught an extra closing parenthesis and removed a redundant error-type expression.  It also corrected the fixture's replay branch to copy its dynamic-extent rest spine before returning that data.  Returning the original DX spine would violate the declaration.  Add a separate verified stack-rest case whose constructed spine survives the old activation while its payload objects remain heap objects.  This establishes spine copying, not promotion of arbitrary stack-allocated payloads.

### Stack-object transfer lifetime review: 2026-10-15

Reviewed the transfer adapters, FRAME-RETURN-CONTEXT, active prompt-stack links, DX allocation/root scanning, and the existing runtime DYNAMIC-EXTENT-P predicate.  The adapters reuse the selected activation's storage and preserve the caller's continuation.  The collector scans surviving DX allocations through their original stack roots.  There is no general object-promotion operation.  [Common Lisp DYNAMIC-EXTENT](https://www.lispworks.com/documentation/HyperSpec/Body/d_dynami.htm) requires its otherwise-inaccessible objects to become inaccessible when their declared extent ends.  A declaration does not authorize retaining an object after unwinding its allocating scope.

First test the defined lifetime case: a caller allocates an actual DX cons, vector, or lexical closure, passes it through the selected callee, and continues to own it after Return/Reinvoke.  Require exact identity/content, actual stack allocation, selected cleanup/full GC, replacement GC, caller GC, and ordinary/nested prompt stacks.  Keep every observation inside the allocating caller's dynamic extent and return only success from that caller.  This is a separate native fixture using the accepted internal helpers, with no runtime or collector change.  It will establish whether the current transfer preserves surviving stack objects.  It will not establish promotion of objects allocated by the unwound frame.

The caller-owned lifetime fixture passed natively.  It asserted actual stack allocation for conses, vectors, and lexical closures; retained exact identity/content through Return and Reinvoke; ran GC during selected cleanup, replacement execution, and caller continuation; and covered older/younger prompt stacks.  All observations remained inside the allocating caller's declared extent.  The fixture compiled without warnings and left no stops or owned jobs after release.  Evidence: debugger-frame-transfer-lifetimes-native.log.

Recommendation after the defined-lifetime test and language review: retain ordinary Common Lisp dynamic-extent preconditions for frame transfers.  The callable and returned/argument objects must remain valid after the selected unwind.  Copying a supplied list spine preserves its storage without changing payload identity or extending payload extent.  A caller-owned DX object remains valid while its caller's allocating scope survives.  A selected-scope DX object's declared extent ends during unwind, so transferring that object beyond the scope violates its declaration.  General stack-object promotion remains unsupported.  State this limit for Return/Reinvoke rather than implying promotion from the successful spine and caller-owned tests.  The public command will retain these preconditions and still needs its own condition-stop/browser/snapshot acceptance.

### Compiled breakpoint foundation review: 2026-10-15

Reread Genera's [breakpoint and single-step commands, printed pages 234–237](https://www.chai.uni-hamburg.de/~moeller/symbolics-info/documentation/Program-Development-Utilities.pdf#page=240).  Breakpoints repeatedly suspend compiled code, with lexical actions/conditions and explicit Once behavior.  Single Step executes an instruction and steps over calls.  Set Trap On Call supplies the documented way to enter a called function.  The manual warns about suspending system I/O, storage, hardware, and GC functions.  These semantics require more than exposing the existing low-level TF routine.

Reviewed the x86 breakpoint/debug handlers, supervisor single-step controls, low-level special-function wrapper, pager exception callbacks, interrupt-save return construction, Lisp BREAK, and the assembler's existing INT 3 encoding. The [Intel system programming manual](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/868137/325462-089-sdm-vol-1-2abcd-3abcd-4.pdf), exception 3, specifies a saved PC after INT3.  Its debug facilities distinguish INT3 from TF single-step exceptions.  The existing pager callback arranges a Lisp invocation on the faulting thread after preserving its interrupt state.  SIMD exceptions already use this path.

Keep the small exception callback resident, as the pager requires. Intel Volume3B section18.3.1.1 requires the handler to set saved RFLAGS.RF to resume the original instruction.  The processor does not set RF for an instruction breakpoint. ### Pager publication probe: 2026-10-15

The traced combined run passed boundary, scope, hardware and intentional INT3 suites.  The subsequent raw TF suite panicked in SCAN-ERROR with unscannable object #x8F01B99 while SCAVENGE-FULL-SAVE-THREAD scanned a regular stack frame.  The background collection worker had not started. The callback preparation and wake traces showed the expected PC, RBX and argument, with GC NIL at those trace points.  This does not establish the collector panic's cause.

Source review found a publication ordering gap.  The interrupt pager enqueue paths release the pager lock before SAVE-INTERRUPTED-STATE saves the requester's registers.  They retain the global thread lock until the switch restore primitive.  PAGER-THREAD dequeues under only the pager lock.  An already-running pager can therefore process a request before its publisher finishes saving registers.  PAGER-RPC has the same publication order.  WAKE-THREAD acquires the thread lock after request processing, so that acquisition cannot protect earlier callback preparation.

Recommendation: use a bounded private resident probe on a fresh parked-snapshot copy.  Pause the pager immediately after one owned RPC has completed and been woken.  Queue a second owned RPC and hold its publisher before the context save.  Release the paused pager, then observe whether HANDLE-PAGER-REQUEST reaches that second request while the publisher still holds the thread lock.  Before processing the second request, the probe must acquire/release that lock to avoid changing an unfinished save.  Record both saved states and release all owned records.  If confirmed, acquire the existing global thread lock while dequeuing, in pager-lock then thread-lock order, and release both before paging.  Test after snapshot boot.  No causal claim about the preserved panics follows from identifying this gap.

Subsequent captures use the mapped current-stack pages shown by the panic backtrace.

The focused native probe confirmed early processing: PAGER entered the second request while the publisher still held the global thread lock and had not saved its context.  The probe then waited for that lock before processing the RPC, restored the exact original HANDLE-PAGER-REQUEST, joined the owned gate thread, and released the driver/session.  Fourteen private resident probe functions compiled without warnings/failure at DEBUG 1/SAFETY 3/SPEED 1.  Evidence: debugger-pager-publication-probe-native.log. ### Collector panic during wired cons allocation: 2026-10-15

Read-only inspection identified the thread being scanned in the third panic: the GUI manager, not an instruction-step target.  Its saved RIP is #x7FFFDB43C6, at RET in %CALL-ON-WIRED-STACK-WITHOUT-INTERRUPTS.  Its caller stack passes through CALL-WITH-PSEUDO-ATOMIC, %ALLOCATE-FROM-WIRED-AREA-1, %ALLOCATE-FROM-WIRED-AREA, %CONS-IN-WIRED-AREA, CONS-IN-AREA, COPY-LIST-IN-AREA, COPY-NAME-TO-WIRED-AREA and MAKE-THREAD.  The collector's stack shows SCAVENGE-REGULAR-STACK-FRAME passing #x8F01B99 to SCAVENGE-OBJECT/MARK-PINNED-OBJECT and ultimately SCAN-ERROR.  Memory at #x8F01B90 contains header #xE0: +OBJECT-TAG-CONS+ (56), followed by a zero header word and two zero-valued cons fields.  Evidence: debugger-pager-publication-third-panic-allocation.log, third-panic-locals.log and mapped object/stack captures.

The allocator returns an object-tagged pointer to this four-word header before MANGLE-PINNED/WIRED-CONS produces the cons-tagged pointer to its final two words.  Its pseudo-atomic interval ends while that temporary object-tagged value remains live.  TYPE-OF recognizes that representation as PINNED-CONS, and heap walking already handles its four-word format.  SCAN-OBJECT-1 lacks its tag case, so a major collection in that interval reaches SCAN-ERROR.  This explains the observed third panic's immediate collector failure.  No causal relationship to the wrong hardware callback or first panic has been established.

Recommendation: add the missing +OBJECT-TAG-CONS+ case to SCAN-OBJECT-1 and scan its four words through SCAN-GENERIC.  Both header words are immediate values; the last two are car/cdr.  Preserve allocation, the cons representation and mark-bit identity.  Test a deliberately retained object-tagged header through full GC for pinned and wired allocations, moving car/cdr identity, shared references through both header-tagged and cons-tagged roots in both traversal orders, and ordinary cons construction.  Use native Mezzano.  The preserved panic supplies the failing case; do not panic the healthy pager candidate to repeat it.

The user's instruction to continue approves the described cons-header scanner correction.  Implement that case and its native tests while preserving the distinct pager and earlier callback-failure scopes.

The scanner compiled/loaded, then test compilation entered an owned reader-error stop before test execution.  Abort/release that owned stop and job, correct the delimiter, and require successful checks before launching the corrected driver.  Preserve the failed log and cleanup evidence.

### Breakpoint management design: 2026-10-15

Review: the retained kernel descriptors already identify an exact compiled function and byte offset, support idempotent installation, and retain a hit after removal/reuse.  The ordinary validator has authoritative instruction maps.  The existing world-stop operation serializes table changes and acknowledges online CPUs.  Genera's Program Development Utilities, printed pages 234–237, specifies function/PC Set and Clear, Clear All for one function (defaulting to the selected function in the debugger), a global Show list, and Single Step over calls: https://www.chai.uni-hamburg.de/~moeller/symbolics-info/documentation/Program-Development-Utilities.pdf .

Recommendation: retain function-object identity plus offset, without a second ID table.  Add ordinary Lisp SET-BREAKPOINT (function offset), CLEAR-BREAKPOINT (function offset), CLEAR-ALL-BREAKPOINTS (function), and BREAKPOINTS ().  SET returns a fresh (function offset) list and is idempotent for that identity/location.  CLEAR returns a Boolean.  CLEAR-ALL returns the removed count.  BREAKPOINTS returns a fresh list of (function offset) pairs.  SET validates instruction metadata before calling the resident installer.  Removal uses exact existing descriptors and does not require metadata to remain available.  Add one resident bulk-clear helper using the current world-stop interval and one synchronization, so concurrent observers cannot see a partially cleared function.  Reuse the four existing slots and all existing locks/fields.

The following command increment will use Set Breakpoint FUNCTION PC, Clear Breakpoint FUNCTION [PC], Clear All Breakpoints [FUNCTION], and Show Breakpoints.  Set requires both operands.  Clear defaults PC to byte 16.  Clear All requires a function in the Listener and defaults to the exact selected executing function in the debugger.  Function operands name symbols or SETF function names, read as one form with read-time evaluation disabled in the owner's current package.  They resolve the current definition once when the accepted command executes.  Direct Lisp calls accept exact function objects, including an older active definition.  Redefinition leaves existing locations on their original functions.  Displayed functions distinguish definitions through their printed identity.  PCs accept decimal or #x hexadecimal byte offsets, as Show Compiled Code displays.  Parser support will add ordered positional operands while preserving existing single-argument commands.

Retained operations will be :SET-BREAKPOINT/:CLEAR-BREAKPOINT with (function-source integer), :CLEAR-ALL-BREAKPOINTS with a string or NIL selected-function default, and :BREAKPOINTS without an argument.  Copy accepted strings/lists and compare replay arguments with EQUAL.  Return guest-formatted text through existing command I/O/results.  Python validates transport types; browser menus and completed-text captions extend their existing lists.  Conditions/actions and Single Step remain separate increments.  No library or new transport type is required.

- [x] Document supported syntax, offsets, identity/redefinition, capacity, and remaining limits.  Core commands pushed as b62f48c7 and Slime protocol documentation as 664634d9.

Compile the focused ordinary fixture and test validation, duplicate/four-slot behavior, independent list snapshots, removal counts, definition replacement and an inspected retained hit after removal. ### Instruction step-over foundation: 2026-10-16

Genera's Program Development Utilities, printed pages 235 and 237, defines Single Step as one instruction with function calls executed as one step.  Intel SDM Volume 3B, section 20.3.1.4, describes TF as a post-instruction trap, including entry into callees and special handling of interrupt/SS instructions: https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/874250/253669-090-sdm-vol-3b.pdf .  The existing Mezzano TF primitive already saves/restores raw stopped threads and passed CALL/RET tests.  The retained BREAK callback cannot call that blocking primitive on its own running thread.  Retained integration therefore remains a following increment.

Recommendation for the next bounded increment: add a resident subtype of the existing instruction-breakpoint descriptor for a temporary call-return location.  It retains an owning thread and the pre-call stack pointer.  The existing four register slots and synchronization serve both kinds.  An unmatched temporary hit sets RF and resumes.  A matching temporary hit saves a raw stopped thread through STOP-THREAD-FOR-SINGLE-STEP.  Prefer a matching temporary descriptor when a public breakpoint shares its address, retain that public descriptor in the step result, and leave its installation intact.  Ordinary installation/listing/function clearing operate only on public descriptors.  Private removal uses the exact descriptor and the existing clear operation.  No thread-layout change, registry, new lock, code mutation, or library is needed.

An ordinary internal SINGLE-STEP-OVER-THREAD helper will decode the exact saved instruction with the existing disassembler.  Non-CALL instructions use the existing TF primitive.  CALL installs a temporary breakpoint at the following validated instruction, resumes the raw stopped target and waits through the existing state protocol, then removes its descriptor in UNWIND-PROTECT.  It returns a coincident public breakpoint descriptor when present.  Slot exhaustion must leave the target stopped and the table unchanged.  A call that exits by a nonlocal transfer may not reach its return location.  Cancellation removes the private descriptor but does not choose how to resume the target.  These constraints must remain explicit until retained integration handles command lifetime and interruption.

- [x] Repeat existing hardware, raw-TF, INT3 and public command fixtures after resident publication.
- [x] Review results and document the internal primitive's scope before commit/push.
- [ ] Design retained command continuation, cancellation and nonlocal transfer handling after this foundation passes.

### Managed TF trap delivery: 2026-10-16

The current #DB handler sends every TF trap to the raw thread-stop primitive.  A retained debugger needs ordinary Lisp entry after the stepped instruction, with TF cleared before that entry executes.  Calling the blocking raw step primitive on the owning thread cannot provide this transition.

Recommendation for the next bounded increment: add resident per-thread instruction-step requests, linked through a resident global and mutated under the existing world-stop mechanism.  Each request retains its target thread, ordinary delivery function and argument.  A matching TF trap clears TF, sets RF, marks the request trapped and uses the existing pager callback path.  The ordinary-context delivery removes the exact request before calling its function.  Cancellation removes only that request and suppresses delivery if it wins before the callback takes ownership.  Raw TF traps without a request retain their existing behavior.  This adds no thread slots, locks, hardware-register consumption, code mutation, or dependencies.  Callers remain responsible for arming/clearing TF only in a stable saved context.  Retained command preparation and transfer are a subsequent increment.

Fill all four public locations to verify TF routing consumes no slot.  Repeat the unchanged raw-TF, call step-over and typed hardware/INT3 fixtures after guarded publication.  Do not expose a Single Step command or claim Genera call step-over from this foundation.

### Retained instruction-step transition: 2026-10-16

The managed TF path now supplies ordinary entry after an instruction.  The next bounded increment will add a native retained :SINGLE-STEP operation, without a Command Processor or Web command.  Its initial instruction acceptance is NOP, direct JMP and RET at a typed native trap's selected interrupted frame.  Other instructions report unsupported before resumption. Add one ordinary private exit-function slot to INSTRUCTION-TRAP and a hidden transfer restart around its debugger entry.  The restart is applicable only to the original condition after preparation supplies that function.  It unwinds the old service before the exit function arms TF in the original saved interrupt flags.  The exit function cancels on another unwind.  A command Abort cancels preparation and leaves the old stop active.  An unexpected debugger entry while :STEPPING cancels the pending request, clears TF only in a matching live interrupt frame, and refreshes the same level.  Leaving CALL-WITH-DEBUGGER-SERVICE closes any stepping record on its thread.  Use the existing service lock for state and the resident request API for routing.  Keep allocation/inspection outside the world-stop critical sections.

Further source review found that relative control transfers and indirect RIP-memory transfers share the same operand class.  PRINT-INSTRUCTION explicitly notes that lost distinction and can print an indirect target as direct code.  Intel's JMP reference distinguishes relative displacement from r/m64 indirect addressing: https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/835757/325383-sdm-vol-2abcd.pdf .  Recommendation: add a RELATIVE-ADDRESS subclass of EFFECTIVE-ADDRESS for DECODE-JB/JZ, preserving their existing base/displacement readers.  The printer will use that type to distinguish code addresses from RIP-memory operands, including labelled memory.  The step validator will accept the relative operand type. Do not classify branch form by rereading opcode bytes in the debugger.

### Ordinary retained-step instructions: 2026-10-16

The compiler emits PUSH RBP, MOV64 RBP/RSP, SUB64 stack allocation and MOV64 root initialization before its body.  The existing retained validator rejects those operations, so its accepted NOP/JMP/RET cases cannot step through an ordinary function entry.  Intel SDM volume 3B section 20.3.1.4 defines post-instruction TF delivery and identifies instructions that suppress or clear it: https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/874250/253669-090-sdm-vol-3b.pdf .  The decoder distinguishes segment-register MOV as MOVSEG.

Recommendation: extend the existing explicit instruction acceptance to PUSH, POP, MOV32, MOV64, LEA64, ADD64, SUB64, CMP64, TEST64, LEAVE, and direct-relative JZ/JNZ.  Retain the existing IF-set/TF-clear and selected interrupted-frame requirements.  MOVSEG, flags/interrupt-control instructions, CALL and other operations remain rejected before preparation.  Reuse the existing managed request, transfer, cancellation and capture paths.  No new kernel representation or command is proposed.

Repeat the complete retained lifetime suite and existing managed/call/typed suites after ordinary publication.  Preserve failed runs and verify empty owned state and protected process fingerprints before committing.  CALL/nonlocal-exit design and public command integration remain following work.

### Managed private call-return delivery: 2026-10-16

Source review found a smaller return-delivery mechanism than adding a second call-request registration.  CLEAR-INSTRUCTION-BREAKPOINT atomically removes an exact descriptor under the existing world-stop protocol and returns whether it removed one.  Private descriptors already retain thread identity and pre-call stack pointer, ignore other-thread/recursive hits, share the four hardware slots, and preserve a coincident public location.

Recommendation: add a resident CALLBACK-INSTRUCTION-STEP-BREAKPOINT subtype with readonly callback and argument slots.  Keep the existing descriptor and request layouts unchanged.  Add an internal constructor/installer using the existing private table.  A matching ordinary-thread, IF-set hit queues a resident pager-delivery function.  That function clears the exact private descriptor before invoking its ordinary Lisp callback.  A cancelled or already delivered descriptor cannot invoke the callback again.  A matching hit in an unsupported delivery context retains the existing raw-stop path.  Descriptor removal controls single delivery through the existing table.  No registry, lock, thread field, transport operation or code mutation is added.

Test normal and recursive returns at zero/two prompts, initial exact PC/flags and caller values, moving callback arguments, duplicate delivery, public/private coincidence and full capacity, two targets and non-owner hits, cancellation before return and before callback acquisition, callback error/Abort, and cleanup. Do not enable retained CALL or expose Single Step from this foundation.

Full CALL behavior still requires a defined nonlocal landing and debugger-error lifetime.  %%UNWIND-TO receives only a special-stack head, which does not identify a GO target.  The compiler's nonlocal context contains its target table, saved SSP, RSP and RBP.  Backend GO lowering obtains the index from TAGBODY-INFORMATION-GO-TAGS, and RETURN uses index zero.  Entry restores SP/FP before ordinary target instructions.  Further review must preserve values, cleanup, prompt-stack identity and normalized frame state before choosing a notification/landing design.  Current Return/Reinvoke also reject frames across an interruption boundary; their condition-stop acceptance remains the documented scope.

The fixture uses its own assembled caller, recording the callee's three returned values after the callback resumes.  Its temporary RAX state pointer uses the assembler's existing :EXTRA-REGISTERS :RAX metadata, so collection can update that pointer.  Structure review found wired layouts/compatible vectors and the runtime's parent-based subtype test, which avoids pageable class-precedence lists.  Before publishing the new interrupt handler, verify the new class, layout, compatible vector, predicate and delivery function addresses are resident.  Publish CPU/interrupt code at DEBUG 1/SAFETY 3/SPEED 1 with existing CPU/hook identity guards.  Compile/load the fixture ordinarily at DEBUG 3/SAFETY 3/SPEED 1.

### Native breakpoint frame transfers: 2026-10-16

Further review: compiler/backend/x86-64/target.lisp declares every allocatable general, MMX and SSE register clobbered by a Lisp call.  Returning or reinvoking an established frame therefore uses the existing calling convention rather than restoring the abandoned instruction's register values.  The partial-save return thunk separately restores FPU state, which includes mutable MXCSR modes.  A transfer that bypasses that thunk must recover the interrupted FPU environment before running application cleanup.

Track the outermost recognized interruption crossed before the selected frame.  Its saved FPU area follows the SS slot in the existing partial-save layout.  Return/Reinvoke restore it through the existing FXRSTOR function before %%UNWIND-TO, allowing application cleanup to restore its caller's modes. ### Native nonlocal-exit context review: 2026-10-16

Review: FORCE-CALL-ON-THREAD converts a full saved context into the existing partial-save return frame, and normal return restores its saved FPU state.  Selected-frame Return/Reinvoke now supply explicit boundary restoration.  Compiler-generated nonlocal GO/RETURN-FROM and runtime THROW still call one-argument %%UNWIND-TO, then bypass the native return thunk.  Retained CALL stepping remains disabled until its nonlocal-exit and error lifetime is defined.  The Genera manual specifies CALL step-over for Single Step and exit trapping when THROW crosses a frame: [Program Development Utilities, sections 5.4.5–5.4.6](https://www.chai.uni-hamburg.de/~moeller/symbolics-info/documentation/Program-Development-Utilities.pdf).

Recommendation: first run a compiled Lisp diagnostic using the existing owned native target.  Under zero/two prompts, change only the debugger's current rounding mode, then compare Proceed and Abort.  Capture exact selected context, returned values/completion, live program bindings, cleanup order and each cleanup's observed rounding mode.  Proceed supplies the saved-context reference behavior.  Abort must be observed before choosing a runtime correction.  Run only on candidate 4014, use ordinary test allocation and existing dependencies, preserve the current fourteen-process baseline, and leave no owned stops/locations/jobs.

A possible native-entry UNWIND-PROTECT needs source review before adoption.  FORCE-CALL-ON-THREAD also serves raw stepping and unsleeping, and its existing callers expect direct entry at the requested function.  A global wrapper would change that API.  No wrapper, compiler hook, dynamic marker, or new thread/frame field is proposed yet.  Preserve the current compiler's late GO-index calculation if later notification needs a destination PC.

Proceed at zero/two prompts restored TARGET cleanup to :POSITIVE-INFINITY after the debugger changed its mode to :NEAREST.  Abort instead ran TARGET cleanup in :NEAREST in both cases.  MIDDLE cleanup ran in :NEGATIVE-INFINITY after TARGET restored its saved caller mode.  Program bindings/order/counts were correct, and the independent audit passed empty owned state and all fourteen current process fingerprints.  Evidence: debugger-native-unwind-probe.log and debugger-native-unwind-probe-audit.log.  This demonstrates native nonlocal unwinding bypassing saved FPU restoration.

### Cold-bootstrap disassembler package ordering

The clean SBCL bootstrap failed while reading SINGLE-STEP-OVER-THREAD in system/debugger-service.lisp: package MEZZANO.DISASSEMBLE.X86-64 did not exist.  No image was created.  The architecture package is defined at the top of system/disassemble-x86-64.lisp, which IPL loads after the cold generator has already compiled the warm debugger service.  compiler/package.lisp creates the shared disassembler package and both assembler packages early, but omits this required architecture package.  The failed host exception is PACKAGE-DOES-NOT-EXIST during INTERN of INST-OPCODE.  Source/version, exact arguments, exit status 1 and full backtrace remain in debugger-clean-build-77d122ff.py/.json/.log.

Recommendation: move the existing x86-64 disassembler DEFPACKAGE, unchanged, into compiler/package.lisp immediately after the shared disassembler package.  Remove its former definition from the implementation file.  This gives early users the canonical package and preserves its use list/local nicknames, without loading runtime disassembler code into the bootstrap host or adding a second declaration.  The ARM64 package has no newly introduced early reader dependency and stays unchanged.  Apply the two-file correction in the isolated clone while production source guards remain active.  Preserve the failed generated cache by renaming it, and rebuild with a new empty target cache.  Record the candidate as 77d122ff plus its explicit source diff, rather than claiming the unmodified revision.  Required acceptance is full image creation followed by real cold boot and native package/disassembler/debugger tests in Mezzano.  Transfer the tested correction to debugging after the current production source-pinned browser acceptance releases its source guard.

### Package storage-condition recovery

The diagnostic probe returned raw frame-local objects to SWANK EVAL-AND-GRAB-OUTPUT.  Its print bindings ended before SWANK formatted the return value.  The result contained cyclic structure data, and unbounded structure/list printing overflowed that worker's stack.  Subsequent fresh requests timed out.  GDB shows the worker waiting in SLDB at STACK-OVERFLOW while the SWANK reader, control and listening threads wait for package mutex 0x5088F99.  Both CPUs are in normal %WAIT-FOR-INTERRUPT, not a demonstrated kernel panic.  Earlier debugger/scalar probes had returned.  Future probes must render bounded strings inside their print bindings instead of returning arbitrary object graphs.  Preserve this failed candidate and exact evidence.  The first GDB decoder failed on a binary name, and the next script crossed an unmapped idle-stack boundary.  The corrected per-page capture preserved target, overflow-worker and idle stack pages, and bounded thread scans identify the wait chain.

Source diagnosis: CALL-WITH-PACKAGE-SYSTEM-LOCK releases its mutex around debugger entry for ERROR handlers only.  STACK-OVERFLOW inherits STORAGE-CONDITION, which inherits SERIOUS-CONDITION directly.  Its handler therefore does not run.  Recommendation: change the existing handler specializer to SERIOUS-CONDITION, retaining the current release/reacquire and restarts.  Test ERROR and STORAGE-CONDITION handlers from another thread while the lock owner is stopped, Continue and Abort, identity and mutual exclusion, and lock availability afterward.  No new lock or transport is required.  Preserve owned 923212 for inspection and boot a new working copy of the accepted cold checkpoint at free 4017/1246, requiring all sixteen existing process fingerprints unchanged.  Publish/test the ordinary package-lock function there before continuing CALL tests.  Its checkpoint restore is not new first-boot evidence.  Do not change production 4006.

The package test's first run sampled MUTEX-OWNER and asserted NIL.  An unrelated SWANK indentation thread owned the lock at that instant.  Such a sample does not test whether a stopped target releases the lock.  Its printed owner later shows DEAD because that thread object is mutable.  Recommendation: remove those two global-idleness assertions.  The separately joined observer acquiring the same lock while the target remains stopped tests release directly, and the target checks ownership after Continue.  Preserve the failed test and abort/release only its owned job.  No mutex implementation change follows from this test error.

Abort and Continue each run cleanup once, and all owned stops/job/session are released.  A separate SWANK test signals the concrete STACK-OVERFLOW condition while holding the mutex, receives SLDB entry, sends its normal protocol Abort, and then completes fresh 42 evaluation. The user approved replacing the Python Web server with a server inside Mezzano while preserving the browser interface and HTTP API.  Reviewed the current HTTP adapter, SWANK session implementation, TCP server demo, compiler load policy, and deployment documentation.

Both adapters share the same session and retained-operation implementation.  Evaluation and debugger command execution keep their current threads.

HTTP authority configuration includes the external port so QEMU forwarding can use a different guest port.  Use one request per connection with correct CRLF framing and byte lengths. The adapter review confirmed Jzon's canonical JSON values: true T, false NIL, null CL:NULL, arrays vectors, and objects hash tables.  Preserve false/null distinctions during input validation, then convert service NIL to JSON null as the existing Python adapter does.  Finite operation/command tables avoid interning browser input.  Capture direct-service diagnostic output in the existing diagnostics field.  Reject duplicate security headers and ambiguous body framing.

HTTP framing follows RFC 9112 sections 2, 3, 5, and 6.3: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9112.html.  Bound the request line to 8 KiB, all headers to 32 KiB and 100 fields, body to 1 MiB, and active request workers/backlog to 64.  Use absolute deadlines and one request per connection.  Expected request errors return HTTP failures.  Unexpected worker errors enter the existing retained debugger after an explicit generic 500 response when possible.  This reuses debugger inspection rather than adding a second error registry.

Shared-session extraction retains the current session owner exclusion, opaque handle tables, boot retirement, transient controller release, and typed error replies.  Its SWANK adapter verifies a live connection before supplying that connection as owner.  A transient HTTP request uses a fresh owner.  Test exclusion, reconnection with the same handles, released sessions, unknown/malformed tokens, retained evaluation identity/replay, and unexpected-error propagation in Mezzano before publication.

Shared-service review retained the original WITH-LOCK error boundary.  Its HANDLER-CASE unwinds the session mutex and foothold inhibition before re-signalling an unexpected error.  Entering the retained debugger while holding that mutex would block all clients attempting to inspect the stop.  The first extraction had removed this boundary as redundant.  Source review caught the error before publication of the new SWANK adapter.  Restore the boundary, then test that an outer error handler can acquire the session mutex and that the original condition propagates.

Jzon malformed-input diagnosis: %CALC-POS declares N as (INTEGER 1), but empty string/vector input calls it with zero while constructing JSON-EOF-ERROR.  This raises TYPE-ERROR instead of the intended parse condition.  The loop already handles zero and returns line 1, column 1.  Correct the declaration to (INTEGER 0).

The UTF-8 decoder and its truncated-sequence readers signal untyped SIMPLE-ERROR conditions.  The HTTP adapter must distinguish malformed JSON from implementation faults.  Recommendation after reviewing Jzon's condition constructors: signal the existing JSON-PARSE-ERROR for invalid UTF-8 and JSON-EOF-ERROR for truncated sequences, using unavailable line/column fields because decoding can fail before a character position exists.  Keep direct octet-vector parsing.  Test empty string/vector/span/stream input, invalid continuation and leading bytes, overlong sequences, surrogates, out-of-range values, truncation, and valid Unicode boundaries in compiled Mezzano, then rerun the JSON API/corpus tests and HTTP malformed-body tests.  Maintain this correction in the existing Jzon fork and pin the tested revision.

Timeout review: the native server's :TIMEOUT bounds socket receive/send phases.  The browser retains its existing 20-second fetch deadline for waiting on synchronous service results.  Documentation lookup and private-document reads can perform synchronous filesystem work under the shared session mutex.  A lost HTTP reply preserves accepted operation identities and the normal dispatcher cleanup.  Retain this behavior without adding operation threads or a cancellation registry.  Test lost-reply recovery and document both timeout scopes.

Use the existing ASDF compiler/cache for the optional Web server: MEZZANO-WEB depends on the already-approved Jzon system and loads the ordinary HTTP server and Web adapter.  The shared remote service is part of the ordinary image core.  A six-line loader locates the ASDF definition beside itself. ### Closed TCP connection receive race: 2026-10-17

The serial log records :CLOSED falling through TCP4-CONNECTION-RECEIVE's ECASE in a loopback packet callback.  Source review establishes two ways to reach it: ABORT-CONNECTION sets :CLOSED before its queued detach runs, and a receive can capture a connection before another thread closes it while receive waits for that connection's mutex.  The loopback callback logs and catches this error.  This trace establishes neither a stopped network queue nor the cause of the measured GC pauses.

After reviewing [RFC 9293, CLOSED segment processing](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293.html#section-3.10.7.1) and the existing unknown-connection branch, use one shared CLOSED-segment helper for both paths.  Ignore an incoming RST.  Otherwise send a reset with the required sequence/acknowledgment fields, returning before normal connection timer updates.  Correct the existing branch's ACK flag and include data, SYN, and FIN in segment sequence length modulo 2^32.  Reuse that sequence-length helper in the existing acceptability check.  No exception suppression or connection revival is needed.

The retransmit timer also checks expiry before taking the connection mutex and omits :CLOSED, permitting a stale callback after abort.  Move expiry checks under the existing mutex in the retransmit and timeout callbacks.  The retransmit callback must disarm and return for :CLOSED.  Test abort while receive/timer callbacks wait for the mutex and rearming while a callback waits, using private connections/interfaces and exact packet assertions.  A deterministic event-gated test must exercise lookup, closure, receive, queued detach, and cleanup.  Existing half-close, timeout, HTTP, and HTTPS tests must follow.  This is a separate kernel-network increment; the RAM comparison continues unchanged.

The timeout callback must also disarm and return immediately for :CLOSED, before constructing a new timeout condition or notifying waiters.  Otherwise an expired callback after abort overwrites the retained CONNECTION-ABORTED condition.  Both callbacks use the same existing connection mutex and preserve the abort outcome.

### High-memory ATA transfers: 2026-10-17

The 4 GiB restore reached SWANK after a slow startup.  Its page-in sample used ATA-PIO-DATA-IN for a 65,536-byte request whose decoded physical buffer was #x10E5F0000.  ATA-READ-WRITE permits direct DMA below 4 GiB, bounces exactly one 4 KiB request, and otherwise uses PIO.  The physical allocator prefers high pages, so the larger guest exposes this path.  No 4 GiB GC result is available yet.  The fixed-heap collection trial is now submitted once and remains independent of source changes.

After reviewing the existing bounce allocation and [Intel's PIIX/PIIX3 descriptor specification, page 99](https://www.alldatasheet.com/html-pdf/66091/INTEL/82371SB/12964/99/82371SB.html), enlarge the existing DMA32 buffer to sixteen pages and transfer ATA requests in chunks of at most 64 KiB.  Use direct DMA only when the whole chunk is addressable.  Otherwise copy the exact chunk through that buffer with the existing word-copy primitive.  Copy a read only after success and stop at the first failure.  The one-page alternative requires sixteen commands and completion waits per normal pager cluster.  Keep the existing controller frame slot and allocator API.

A PRD must stay within a physical 64 KiB boundary, use zero for a 64 KiB byte count, and set EOT only on its final entry.  Correct the existing length-only splitting and reserved-bit write.  Tests must cover descriptor boundaries/counts, exact partial and multi-chunk copies, whole-range DMA eligibility, failures, real low/high-memory transfers on a disposable disk, and snapshot restoration.  The current ATA implementation and test disk use 512-byte sectors.  Existing controllers own only one bounce page, so publishing code that assumes sixteen pages into the running image would be unsafe.  Compile the revised resident driver into a new cold image and initialize its controllers normally.  Keep the tested production image unchanged while this kernel increment is tested.

A 32-bit register destination clears its upper half, while a 32-bit memory destination retains adjacent bytes.  Tests must distinguish those results.

### Logical fixture allocation failure: 2026-10-19

The first native attempt stopped after forty completed cases (24 AND32, 16 AND64).  The kernel panic says: Trying to acquire mutex Allocator while pseudo-atomic. ### Stop inspection latency: source review

The full-body Chromium run exposed the cost of automatic inspection after every step.  APP.JS refreshes through a 1500 ms interval.  REFRESH reads retained results and INSPECTSELECTEDSTOP submits one of frames/restarts/condition/current-frame.  MUTATE records that accepted command but schedules no immediate refresh, so later inspections advance through later timer polls.  This is a product scheduling delay, in addition to the test's typed Show Instruction and independent native-oracle jobs.

Reviewed proposal: enqueue one immediate REFRESH through the existing serialized action queue after an automatic inspection submission succeeds.  That refresh reads its result and may submit the next inspection.  If the result remains pending, ordinary timed polling continues.  Keep separate retained inspection commands and their failure boundaries.  A combined display operation would require new result handling and could discard useful partial inspection when a printer fails, so the smaller queue change is preferable.  The 1500 ms poll interval and HTTP deadlines stay as they are.

Required tests: terminal and deliberately pending inspections, nested printer failure/Abort, queued user commands, generation transitions, and absence of repeated immediate refresh when a command remains pending.  Compare measured step-to-complete-inspection timing through Chromium.  The current AGENTS decision procedure authorizes this reviewed recommendation.  A host-only draft adds RUN(REFRESH) after successful automatic inspection submission.  Because RUN appends to the existing promise queue without awaiting the queued action, it preserves user-action order and avoids awaiting its own active queue entry.  The next refresh queues another only if it submits a new inspection.  A pending command queues none and remains on ordinary timed polling.  No product source or active assets have changed; the current browser run continues against unchanged assets.

### Argument display and dynamic-extent review

The initial recommendation was a no-argument Show Rest Argument command using the existing current-parameter reader and Show Function history pattern.  [Genera's command description, printed page 212](https://www.chai.uni-hamburg.de/~moeller/symbolics-info/documentation/Program-Development-Utilities.pdf#page=218), displays the current rest value and assigns *.  SERVICE-FRAME-PARAMETER-CONTEXT already identifies the exact source rest descriptor, distinguishes available NIL from absent storage, and reads lexical or exact special cells.  No new argument-reconstruction primitive is required for its established x86-64 frame scope.

The whole-path review found a lifetime case that must precede this command.  Source inspection shows that normal DEBUG 3 lexical rest retains its heap COPY-LIST because preserved BIND-LOCAL use prevents automatic dynamic-extent conversion.  An explicit DYNAMIC-EXTENT declaration omits that copy.  X86-64 EMIT-DX-ARGUMENT-LIST stores its spine in the callee's dynamic stack, with a GC-visible DX root.  GC scans its heap-element references but leaves the stack pointer unchanged.  The separate original-argument reader copies its own hidden spine before returning it.  Relevant sources are compiler/backend/convert-ast.lisp, compiler/backend/ssa.lisp, compiler/backend/passes.lisp, compiler/backend/x86-64/codegen.lisp, system/gc.lisp, and the dynamic-extent layout in the ABI reference.

Existing frame evaluation can place an observed value directly in evaluation history.  Stepping clears Inspector maps but preserves that history.  LEAVE discards the callee's dynamic stack before RET.  This identifies a possible existing escape through history.  No native dangling-value failure has been demonstrated.  The revised recommendation is to test live storage and retention before implementing the display command.  Use two ordinary SAFETY 3/DEBUG 3/SPEED 1 targets, normal and explicitly dynamic-extent rest.  While established, check storage bounds, exact binding identity, emitted allocation/copy behavior and heap-element identity through moving collection.  Retain only numeric address observations outside that activation.  Use the existing safe split-word capture if a raw integer would otherwise allocate in pseudo-atomic context.  Test history across LEAVE/RET only for the proven heap value.  For the DX case, clear all raw history and Inspector references before LEAVE, then finish without retaining or dereferencing its former spine.  This diagnostic establishes the live representation without creating a dangling GC root.  Any implementation correction requires the resulting evidence and another whole-path review.  The clean UI release precedes this probe.

### Exact parameter type metadata review

The next writable-argument work can reuse SERVICE-FRAME-VARIABLE, its owning-thread/generation checks, exact storage readers, declaration checks and representation-aware setter.  Exact special parameters require resolving their saved binding cells, and register-only writes remain unsupported.  An Inspector object token cannot replace a frame binding reference.  Genera's argument locative and DBG:ARG operations therefore require a live parameter reference and a controlled value accessor.

Independent source review found that the compiler retains the information needed for declaration-safe references.  EXTEND-ENVIRONMENT stores types by binding identity and preserves shadowed entries.  DEBUG-SOURCE-SCOPE removes those entries when building name-visible :variables.  A parameter declaration captured only at entry would miss a LOCALLY narrowing that remains applicable before a later same-name binding.  Do not borrow the shadow's type, infer from the value or storage, or scan other PCs.  The existing environment explicitly records T for an undeclared new lexical binding.  An absent type-table entry and a present entry whose type is NIL remain distinct.

The final recommendation is a :PARAMETER-TYPES list in each current-PC scope, keyed by existing lexical descriptors or the special parameter's saved-cell descriptor.  Each entry is (descriptor type), read by EQ from that instruction's compiler type table.  Missing binding/type data remains unavailable.  A known zero-parameter layout produces an empty list.  Missing parameter context uses :UNKNOWN.  Visible :variables, shared descriptor shapes, the seven-element parameter layout, locations and GC representation stay unchanged.  Pass source parameter context through DEBUG-SOURCE-SCOPE and its cache recursion from both architecture emitters, whose caches are local to one backend function.  Existing scope serialization preserves descriptor identity.

PASS1-LAMBDA-INNER currently records parameter objects, then supplies fresh SPECIAL-VARIABLE objects while extending the body environment for SPECIAL declarations.  The source-parameter record and body type declarations can consequently name different compiler objects.  Remove that redundant :variables construction and use EXTEND-ENVIRONMENT's existing :declarations processing, which reuses an explicit special binding.  PASS1-LOCALLY-BODY already follows that route.  This corrects the compiler identity relationship rather than teaching the debugger to match unrelated same-name objects.
