### Snapshot/collection phase correction recommendation

Read-only GDB confirms 409172 block reservations plus the fixed 256-page margin equals the reported fudge 409428 exactly.  There is no reservation-counter drift in this failure.  The general destination already has 57344 lazy pages, so GC passed its first allocation and failed the cons destination.  It needed 205824 pages with 202514 available: a 3310-page shortage before the cons card allocation.  Undoing the new general allocation/cards reconstructs pre-collection available bytes 1064837120 versus required reserve 1089835008.  Snapshot had made the allocator's reserve negative before collection began.

The requesting thread was a MANAGER allocating COPY-LIST in WAIT-FOR-OBJECTS, blocked in SLOW-CONS/%GC.  Background GC was sleeping.  SNAPSHOT-BML1 makes committed pages require replacement reservations without GC admission, and TAKE-SNAPSHOT resumes ordinary threads during writeout while retaining old Snapshot disk blocks until header commit.  A normal allocation then requests collection before those blocks become free.  The collector currently has no phase exclusion.

Final recommendation after independent review: add one resident prepared-writeout flag.  Set it at the end of TAKE-SNAPSHOT's existing world-stop, after block-map/freelist preparation and before ordinary threads resume.  Clear it after header commit and deferred-block release.  GC-WORKER, after acquiring the world and before setting GC-IN-PROGRESS, flipping semispaces or timing the collection, waits on the existing Snapshot-completion event when this flag is true.  A requested but inhibited Snapshot has no prepared writeout and therefore does not prevent GC.  Clear the phase flag in INITIALIZE-SNAPSHOT before signaling its preserved completion event.

This uses the existing event and scheduler rules.  Snapshot/disk/pager supervisor threads keep running while GC owns the stopped world.  Successful post-capture writeout uses preallocated requests, bounce/PRDT storage and raw physical metadata allocation, with no normal allocating helper or second world-stop.  Finalizers remain outside the collection extent.  A new mutex or enlarged GC-LOCK extent would save Snapshot ownership whose release frame is discarded when the ephemeral thread restarts.  The phase/event design avoids that ownership problem.

Required tests: hold real writeout on a bounded resident gate, request collection, verify the collector waits before semispace/GC counters change, release writeout and require commit/reclamation followed by collection.  Test a requested/inhibited Snapshot whose caller still needs GC, then normal completed-state save/restore and repeated allocation/collection with reservation counts.  Preserve the current panicked image/process before recovery.  The phase correction addresses concurrent collection during prepared writeout.  It does not prove that every heap can fit an arbitrarily small store.

Source review also found a separate diagnostic counter defect: STORE-DEFERRED-FREE omits its count increment when coalescing, and STORE-RELEASE-DEFERRED-BLOCKS omits the decrement.  Its global value cannot quantify this Snapshot's detached list.  Review/fix that counter in a separate bounded increment, counting actual ranges for the current diagnosis.

The detached Snapshot list was recovered from TAKE-SNAPSHOT's saved RBP−0x60 slot.  Its 7409 ranges contain 323991 blocks (1327067136 bytes).  The global deferred list is NIL, while its diagnostic counter says 7409.  Native disassembly and destination mappings confirm the failed cons allocation.  Header commit/reclamation would release enough space for this case.

### Deferred-store release correction recommendation

Independent review and root source inspection confirm two accounting omissions: STORE-DEFERRED-FREE counts a new range but omits adjacent additions, and STORE-RELEASE-DEFERRED-BLOCKS omits subtraction.  STORE-STATISTICS documents blocks as its third value.  The count must include both the global deferred list and a detached Snapshot batch until release.  Detachment and temporary freelist serialization do not change that count.

Release also leaks each detached range's metadata node.  REGENERATE-STORE-FREELIST passes numeric ranges into the main freelist without transferring these separate nodes.  SNAPSHOT-FREELIST transfers their list to TAKE-SNAPSHOT, and the release function is its only consumer.  No later path returns them to FREELIST-FREE-METADATA.

Final recommendation after whole-path review: increment once after every successful defer insertion or merge.  In release, save the next node and numeric range, free its blocks, subtract its length, return its metadata node, and advance through the saved next pointer.  Returning metadata overwrites NEXT, so traversal must retain that pointer first.  This consumes the detached list.  It corrects diagnostic counts and metadata ownership without changing the page-reservation policy or the collection exclusion.

Use a resident native probe with a guarded twelve-block allocation under the existing VM write lock.  Prefill metadata before recording baselines.  Force new, prepend and append transitions, detach an owned two-node batch while preserving unrelated deferred ranges, add a third owned global node, and release the old batch.  Require the new node/count to remain.  Release it and unused guards.  Compare exact deferred/free-block/free-metadata baselines and original global head after cleanup.  Record numeric results under the lock and assert from ordinary Lisp afterward.  A resident idle-only reconciliation helper must sum the existing global list during publication under Snapshot inhibition and VM write lock, because historical counts are already wrong.

### TCP send-window correction recommendation

The filtered guest trace recorded 199 packets without overflow.  Peer window 65535 accompanied outstanding data growing from 78920 to 170224 bytes.  The peer later advertised 488 and zero at ACK 1175360318 while SND.NXT was 1175370863.  Subsequent 61400/65535 window reopenings did not send the missing tail.  ACK progress then followed individual backed-off retransmissions.  This establishes violation of the advertised send window and explains this incomplete document response.  Earliest-segment retransmission and exponential timeout backoff follow RFC 6298 and remain in place.

The observer restored the original top-level receiver before failing its final closure-identity assertion.  Preserve that diagnostic failure separately from the 199 packet records.  Root inspected its condition/restarts/frames, saved all records, and aborted/released only the observer's owner stop/job/session.  Source review identified generic lambda value propagation as a candidate for the failed identity check.  Two isolated native DEBUG 1/SAFETY 3/SPEED 1 witnesses both returned NIL where the same stored closure must compare EQ.  The first attempted combined witness had an unmatched parenthesis and failed reading before compilation.  The balanced witness and its results are preserved separately.

Review and revision favor an unsent-data queue over blocking TCP-SEND.  Keep the existing copy-and-return API and connection mutex.  Add peer window/update sequence tracking, pending owned octet data and a close-requested flag.  Transmit only within the advertised usable window, drain queued data on valid ACK/window progress, and defer FIN until all pending data is transmitted.  Reject new application writes after close is requested.  Retransmission entries represent transmitted sequence space only.  Use the existing retransmission timer for bounded one-octet zero-window probes, including recovery when a reopening update is lost.  Process duplicate ACK window updates, partial acknowledgments and sequence wrap correctly.  Avoid adding synchronous write arbitration, HTTP-specific deadline propagation or another asynchronous worker.

Follow [RFC 9293 send-window management](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293.html#section-3.8.6) and [ACK/window processing](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293.html#section-3.10.7.4), plus [RFC 6298 timer rules](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6298.html#section-5).  Do not restart an already-running retransmission timer merely because a later segment is added.  Keep unrelated RTT-estimator findings separate from the current correction.

Required packet-level tests cover bounded initial sends, ACK-driven progress, partial/duplicate/stale updates, zero-window probes/reopening, sequence wrap, copied data ownership, and FIN after all data.  Require existing half-close/closed-stream tests, exact complete large HTTP bodies, and the original Chromium Listener/Debugger/Document Examiner/Peek sequence.  Keep HTTP/browser deadlines and complete document bodies unchanged.

### Stored closure identity correction recommendation

The native witnesses establish incorrect value propagation at DEBUG 1.  A lambda initializer runs once, but the compiler copies it into ordinary value reads, so storing that value and comparing a later read yields NIL.  One syntactic read inside a loop likewise creates distinct closures instead of reading the single stored function.  This violates binding identity.  [FUNCTION](https://www.lispworks.com/documentation/HyperSpec/Body/s_fn.htm) permits separate lambda evaluations to produce distinct closures.  It does not authorize duplicating the evaluation of an initializer used through one binding.

Final recommendation after whole-path review: retain known lambda initializers for direct-call optimization, but prohibit their substitution into ordinary function-valued reads.  Factor the existing substitution bookkeeping into one helper.  An immediate-call helper may use it for the first operand of %FUNCALL/%APPLY and the function operand of AST-MULTIPLE-VALUE-CALL.  Process that operand before other arguments.  Existing lambda lifting then retains direct-call optimization and existing COPY-FORM binding remapping.  Ordinary aliases continue to reference the original binding.  No DEBUG-policy change or new metadata is required.

Cover DEBUG 0/1/3 and compilation-speed 1/3.  Check direct-call lifting in optimized AST and revise the older test that incorrectly expected lambda substitution into an arbitrary value argument.  Run existing environment tests and the original diagnostic observer after clean native compilation.

Zero-window probe review revises the pending-queue plan.  Linux's [TCP output implementation](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/net/ipv4/tcp_output.c), TCP_WRITE_WAKEUP and TCP_XMIT_PROBE_SKB, uses a zero-payload ACK at SND.UNA minus one when no queued byte fits the window.  The receiver rejects that old sequence and reports its current ACK/window.  Root reviewed the primary source.  Use that same probe with the existing backoff timer, leaving SND.NXT, pending offsets and retransmit data unchanged.  This replaces the earlier one-octet plan and handles data-only and deferred-FIN cases without another transmission state.  Require a test proving that a lost reopening update recovers from the probe and then sends the original bytes once.

### Cold pager closure diagnosis and recommendation

Read-only GDB inspection of the failed cold guest recorded CR2 #x8000009E10, the new image map's FULL-/ entry.  The fault occurred in the GC reserve calculation during secondary-CPU stack allocation with the world stopped.  Its pager then attempted a normal general-area allocation and hit the explicit pseudo-atomic prohibition.

Native compilation of the exact pager function, without publishing or executing it, confirms that the complete optimization/lowering pipeline emits MAKE-SIMPLE-VECTOR and MAKE-CLOSURE for GET-LEVEL.  Pass1 represents its three local calls as CL:FUNCALL with lexical-reference callees.  The stored-closure correction recognizes only internal %FUNCALL/%APPLY.  SIMPLIFY subsequently wraps each unresolved CL:FUNCALL callee in %COERCE-TO-CALLABLE, preventing that later propagation.  A simple capturing arithmetic FLET already compiles without allocation, so that case alone fails to cover the pager's captured nonlocal return.

Final recommendation after reviewing pass1, CONSTPROP, SIMPLIFY and lambda lifting: recognize CL:FUNCALL and CL:APPLY alongside the existing internal forms, processing their function operand before argument side effects.  Preserve stored-function reads.  Extend the AST occurrence-scope test to ordinary function-call syntax and test normal FLET calls with a captured BLOCK exit through the complete compiler.  Require no heap allocation at optimized DEBUG 0/1, correct normal/nonlocal results, the full stored-closure and AST suites, and exact pager compilation without closure/vector allocation.  Publish only the changed compiler method, preserving the constant-folder registry.  Do not add a pager allocation declaration to conceal missed call propagation.

### GC reserve arithmetic review

The proposed concern about rational GC reserve allocation is not supported by the area invariants.  Cold serialization aligns every area extent to +ALLOCATION-MINIMUM-ALIGNMENT+, including a fixed aligned wired-function extent.  Pinned/function growth rounds to that same alignment, and STATIC-AREA-SIZE measures those extents rather than object usage.  They divide exactly by the 128 data bytes per bitmap byte.  Native observation measured static size 314572800, modulo 128 zero, an integer reserve and zero allocated bytes.

A separate plain CEILING probe handled zero, byte boundaries and both largest fixnums without allocating, but that does not demonstrate a defect in the existing aligned reserve calculation.  Final recommendation: leave reserve arithmetic unchanged.  The FULL-/ page fault exposed the pager closure-allocation regression.  Require a fresh cold build and boot with the corrected ordinary-callee propagation before claiming that boot failure fixed.  Preserve the first candidate and all probe logs.

### Conditional LLF constant loading failure

The private-source guest reached Bordeaux-Threads 0.9.4's compiled apiv1/default-implementations.lisp while loading cl-video, then IPL panicked.  The error reports integer 1416471921 as the wrong type for LAYOUT.  Preserve PID 1069249/start 89580620, its RAM, working image, source/cache files and serial log.  Native suites and Web acceptance have not started.

Read-only GDB inspection records opcode #x29 (LAYOUT) in LOAD-ONE-OBJECT.  Its class operand is symbol #x1581539 with name INHIBITED-FUNCALL and symbol header #xA8DB4AE2C0.  INSTANCE-SLOT-LOCATION interprets that symbol header as an instance layout, yielding tagged fixnum #xA8DB4AE2, or integer 1416471921.  The symbol is LOAD-ONE-OBJECT's placeholder when it suppresses FUNCALL-N inside an inactive file-level IF.  Class constant reconstruction uses MAKE-LOAD-FORM and a function call, so the suppression also disables the required class lookup before LAYOUT.

Review of both writers, the guest loader and the cold loader shows shared literal backlinks span conditional branches.  Guarding only LAYOUT would preserve an invalid placeholder for later active references.  Moving all literals before the file's definitions would break class-definition order.  Retiring file-level IF also changes the cross-bootstrap's lazy evaluation path and is broader than this correction requires.

Final recommendation: keep serialization order and file-level program conditionals, but evaluate MAKE-LOAD-FORM creation and initialization in a separate, initially empty conditional context.  Add begin/end literal-loading operations around that existing writer path.  Nested literals save and restore the enclosing conditional stack.  The guest loader retains its ordinary branch rules inside each context.  The cold loader already builds lazy conditional forms and forces literal prerequisites, so the new context markers require no evaluation change there.  Bump the LLF version and rebuild compiled files rather than support old files with the defective behavior.

First reproduce the failure with an owned compiled file in the main Mezzano guest.  Then test skipped and active nested conditionals, class layouts and instance headers, shared backlinks, cyclic MAKE-LOAD-FORM initialization, LOAD-TIME-VALUE single evaluation, and propagated creation/initialization errors.  [CLHS LOAD-TIME-VALUE](https://www.lispworks.com/documentation/HyperSpec/Body/s_ld_tim.htm) requires load-time evaluation with a literal result and one evaluation per file load.  Preserve the first failure.  Test the changed writer/loader without reloading module globals, followed by a new cold build, native startup, debugger/TCP suites, browser acceptance and Snapshot/restoration.

### Two-prompt nonlocal restore kernel failure

The zero-prompt saved-image finish passed at 07:10 UTC.  Its log SHA256 is dcc320465bcd8ba91b660a464ac8911d50badd0d001a23cd7a3f6b42eab0a3a7.  The read-only stopped checkpoint SHA256 is 0d4bdaee2457124cb333f9c39697475a70246fbab1cfd837e2e1d94de02014f8.

Serial inspection then found the kernel fault, rather than a completed startup.  FINISH was not invoked. The exact fault is a disabled-interrupt instruction fetch at 0x800001DB10, Common Lisp BYTE in the cold image map.  The VirtIO network worker hit the pending private THROW landing at resident %CATCH while holding the world.  DR6 is 0xffff0ff8 and DR7 is 0x04aa; slot 3 addresses 0x7fff88bb33.  The decoder must identify and ignore this other-thread hit before returning with RF.

GDB disassembly identifies INSTRUCTION-BREAKPOINT-FOR-INTERRUPT's call through BYTE at 0x7fff896443, followed by BYTE-POSITION and BYTE-SIZE.  Its dynamic (BYTE 4 (+ 16 (* index 4))) prevents constant field lowering.  All three functions have pageable bodies; the interrupt handler cannot fetch them on demand.  This explains the observed kernel fault.  Earlier successful cases do not establish that those pageable code pages were absent.

Final recommendation after reviewing the decoder and cold map: shift DR7 right by four times the slot index and extract a constant (BYTE 4 16) field.  Preserve status/enables, PC comparison, thread/SP matching, public/private precedence and RF handling.  Confirm native arithmetic equivalence across all four slots and mode fields, and inspect compiled function references for the three pageable byte-specifier functions.  Add the check to the existing hardware-breakpoint fixture, then build the corrected resident function into a fresh cold image and repeat native breakpoint/step and actual zero/two-prompt restoration tests.  Do not disable restored breakpoints or relax the failing test.  The two-prompt restore remains failed.

The source decoder receives two arguments from its fixed interrupt call site.  Requiring all error-path implementations resident exceeds this valid-path correction.

Revised final recommendation: check that the decoder's direct references contain none of BYTE, BYTE-POSITION or BYTE-SIZE, the pageable functions used by its normal dynamic-field extraction.  Keep the decoder's own resident-placement assertion and the real hardware/restoration tests.  Do not force ordinary error handling into wired memory. Review points to class/layout constants requiring a named class before its own defining form executes.  This remains a hypothesis. The relevant requirements are [top-level processing](https://www.lispworks.com/documentation/HyperSpec/Body/03_bca.htm), [DEFSTRUCT](https://www.lispworks.com/documentation/HyperSpec/Body/m_defstr.htm), and [MAKE-LOAD-FORM](https://www.lispworks.com/documentation/HyperSpec/Body/f_mk_ld_.htm).  Defining forms must have their specified load-time effects in order.  A named class literal resolves through its class name.  Compiler-generated constants must preserve valid source-file loading in a fresh environment.

### ADD32 retained-step increment

Source review finds ADD64 in SERVICE-SINGLE-STEP's ordinary instruction whitelist and ADD32 absent.  The disassembler and assembler already implement ADD32.  Single Step uses hardware TF for this instruction class, so extending the admitted opcode requires no arithmetic emulation, saved-context representation, kernel change, transport change, or dependency.

The [Intel instruction reference, ADD, pages 3-30 through 3-32](https://www.intel.com/content/dam/support/us/en/documents/processors/pentium4/sb/25366621.pdf#page=72) specifies register, immediate and memory forms and the six arithmetic flags.  Final recommendation after comparing the existing SUB32/TEST32 fixture: admit ADD32 through the existing path and extend that fixture with 24 addition targets across the same five operand forms.  Test zero, auxiliary carry, unsigned wrap, both signed-overflow directions, register zero-extension and preservation of adjacent memory bytes at zero/two prompts.  Keep the original 26 targets and six compiled argument-prefix walks.  Require the existing exact-PC, accepted replay, moving-root, value, code-byte and cleanup checks.  Compare the original generated targets' instruction bytes before/after the fixture extension.

### Compiler worker shutdown investigation

COMPILE-FILE queues :FINISHED on success, then requests asynchronous termination without joining its workers.  Its worker-error branch requests termination before signalling the original condition.  The enclosing cleanup requests termination again.  These duplicate requests are established by source inspection.  The cause of the three previously observed stranded workers remains unproven.

CALL-WITH-MUTEX protects acquisition and its body with UNWIND-PROTECT.  ACQUIRE-MUTEX changes state before owner on its fast path.  RELEASE-MUTEX checks owner, clears it, and then changes state or transfers ownership.  Those sequences contain no foothold inhibition.  A second asynchronous exit can abandon cleanup during release.  The dead-owner and NIL-owner observations require separate tests.

The first prepared probe uses an owned raw thread whose cleanup takes and releases a private mutex.  Its kernel hook pauses the loaded release consistency check during that cleanup.  After a second termination request, the coordinator releases the gate and checks thread death, mutex ownership, and mutex state.  A preliminary release verifies that the loaded RELEASE-MUTEX calls the hook.  The hook matches only the owned mutex and target thread.  The original fdefinition restores on exit, and private state remains available for diagnosis.

The hook and its guard cells require resident allocation because the check can run with interrupts disabled.  A separate supervisor module follows the pager-publication kernel fixture's DEFGLOBAL pattern and loads wired.  Nonmatching calls invoke the retained original function through resident cells.  The ordinary fixture uses default allocation.

The two source files and their hash receipt are prepared under WORKER-TERMINATION-20261020.  Native compilation and execution remain pending.  Run them on a separate disposable guest while preserving the browser acceptance candidate.  After the primitive test, use the compiler's return mailbox to test its duplicate-request path.  Normal completion should use THREAD-JOIN.  Error cleanup should request termination once and preserve the original condition.  Any synchronization change requires tests of the exact interruption it corrects.

- [x] Reproduce release-cleanup abandonment during normal-return cleanup and with two termination requests.
- [ ] Test the compiler's duplicate-request path and normal worker shutdown.
- [ ] Correct the diagnosed paths and test condition identity, cleanup, and joined exit.
- [ ] Test acquisition/release interruption before changing kernel synchronization.

### Foothold restoration boundary test

Final recommendation after reviewing WITH-FOOTHOLDS and CALL-WITH-MUTEX: test the existing mask-restoration boundary before changing mutex code.  WITH-FOOTHOLDS currently restores the prior counter in an ordinary UNWIND-PROTECT cleanup.  A second asynchronous exit might abandon that restoration.  Protecting mutex release with this mechanism requires establishing that behavior first.

This inserted gate tests the restoration window.  It changes no shared macro, scheduler function or mutex implementation.  Compile serially and load normally in Mezzano.  Preserve the expansion and results.  A proven restoration gap requires correction before claiming that an outer WITHOUT-FOOTHOLDS makes mutex cleanup safe against repeated interruption.

### Find Frame: reviewed implementation plan

The next command increment follows [Program Development Utilities, printed pages 215–216](https://www.chai.uni-hamburg.de/~moeller/symbolics-info/documentation/Program-Development-Utilities.pdf#page=221).  Genera searches function names, changes the current frame, reverses toward newer frames, and offers Detailed and Invisible options.  The manual does not specify matching case, initial position, wrapping, or a miss.  Mezzano has no hidden-frame classification.

Recommendation after reviewing the frame service, retained-command validation, transports, and browser frame rendering: add one Find Frame operation to the existing command path.  Match a nonempty, case-sensitive substring of the executing definition's name.  Begin after the selected frame, move toward older callers by default or newer callees with Reverse, and stop at the end without wrapping.  A miss returns a message and preserves selection and history.  Reject malformed options before accepting an ID.  Invisible No is accepted.  Invisible Yes reports unsupported hidden-frame classification before acceptance.  Do not infer hidden status from function names or stack positions.

Reuse the current frame result for a match.  Ordinary display includes arguments.  Detailed adds locals and the existing disassembly with its current instruction marked.  Detailed, Reverse, and Invisible default to No when omitted and Yes when mentioned.  Search, printing, and disassembly run in the owning command thread outside the service lock.  Select only after a name matches.  A later printing error follows the existing nested-command debugger behavior.  Retained arguments are copied and compared structurally for replay.  Browser changes render those existing frame fields and the optional code field.

Required tests cover parsing/completion/defaults, forward/reverse duplicate names, boundaries and misses, malformed/replayed/conflicting requests, history preservation, GC and an active old definition after redefinition, detailed output, printer failure and Abort, HTTP validation, and Chromium command entry and selection. This command remains unsupported until its native, transport, and browser tests pass.

### Unused ancestor storage: source review

The pending lexical-ancestry work requires a compiler change.  LOWER-ENVIRONMENT calls DETECT-USES, then computes closure layouts and free-variable sets from executable AST references.  LOCALP uses LEXICAL-VARIABLE-USED-IN.  COMPUTE-FREE-VARIABLE-SETS-1 records only those executable references, and LOWER-ENV-FORM drops an enclosing environment when that set is empty.  Source-environment metadata can therefore describe an unused outer binding while the generated closure retains no storage for it.  Changing only debugger display or only the emitted layout cannot preserve that value.

This was source inspection during the cold instruction matrix.  No compiler change or new supported behavior follows.  A later bounded change must coordinate capture/use analysis and free-variable analysis under the supported debugging policy, retaining binding identity and shared writes.  Review dynamic-extent lifetimes before choosing that change.  Native tests must distinguish live and escaped closures, shadowed variable/function bindings, shared mutation, AST copying/inlining, moving GC, and reduced debugging policies.  Current documented unavailable storage remains accurate.

The lexical-ancestry source review also confirmed a lifetime constraint.  The [Genera command description](https://www.chai.uni-hamburg.de/~moeller/symbolics-info/documentation/Program-Development-Utilities.pdf#page=231) describes lexical ancestors.  The [Common Lisp DYNAMIC-EXTENT declaration](https://www.lispworks.com/documentation/HyperSpec/Body/d_dynami.htm) permits allocation optimizations subject to its lifetime assertion.  Mezzano currently converts supported dynamic-extent initializers before environment lowering.  Adding retained debugger captures only during closure layout could therefore put a stack-allocated value into an escaping debug environment.  The existing test deliberately reports UNUSED as unavailable in an escaped closure.  Preserving that value requires coordinated capture/liveness and allocation decisions before closure layout.

### Desktop-disabled boot: explicit filesystem dependencies

The first boot reached SWANK, then panicked while compiling FILE/EXT4.LISP's DEFPACKAGE: No package named ITERATE.  The exact condition and Lisp stack are preserved in the serial log.  EXT4's package uses ITERATE but its source declares no REQUIRE.  The previous GUI dependency sequence had loaded it indirectly.  The failed guest is unaccepted; native/browser tests have not run.  Do not query its stopped scheduler through SWANK.

Audit of the remaining common warm loads found FILE/HTTP.LISP's top-level REQUIRE of Babel followed by reader-qualified Babel symbols.  That dependency must also exist while compiling the file.  The disassemblers, debugger utilities and HTTP demo use core packages.  Source review establishes no additional GUI dependency in those files.

Final recommendation: declare EXT4's existing Iterate dependency with top-level EVAL-WHEN (:COMPILE-TOPLEVEL :LOAD-TOPLEVEL :EXECUTE), before DEFPACKAGE.  Put HTTP's existing Babel REQUIRE under the same situations.  This loads each component's declared dependency before reading/compiling its dependent forms and supports direct source loading.  It adds no library to the installed set.  The [Common Lisp EVAL-WHEN specification](https://www.lispworks.com/documentation/HyperSpec/Body/s_eval_w.htm) defines these compile/load effects.

Stop only the verified panicked candidate, preserving its raw working disk, serial log, identity, hashes and original source manifest.  Record these as failure evidence, not as a memory snapshot.  Boot a new working copy of the exact pristine fd3e1cf4 cold image.  EXT4 and HTTP are external CAL-loaded modules, outside the embedded warm-source list, so their corrected sources require no new core image.  Record both new source hashes and preimages as an explicit external-source delta.  Reuse the same-core native dependency caches produced by the failed boot, validating their unchanged source manifest.  This retry is a fresh cold-core boot with reused library caches.  Test the corrected components and all original headless requirements.

## Headless native loader correction: 2026-10-21

The retry completed startup in 335.11 seconds, with 48.32 seconds of GC.  Desktop-disabled package/system, process, and arithmetic assertions passed. The [MAKE-PATHNAME specification](https://www.lispworks.com/documentation/HyperSpec/Body/f_mk_pn.htm) specifies the host default. ### Startup error-handling source findings

IPL installs a global debugger that calls PANIC and clears it only at successful completion.  SWANK can therefore be listening while a later filesystem or desktop initialization error panics the guest, as the preserved EXT4 failure demonstrates.  The retained service is already loaded in the warm core before IPL; SWANK becomes the available remote control channel partway through IPL.

LOAD-INIT-FILE catches ERROR, prints the condition, and returns.  RUN-BOOT-HOOKS wraps every early, ordinary, and late hook in LOG-AND-IGNORE-ERRORS.  Those paths discard the failing activation before remote inspection.  POST-BOOT-WORKER runs deferred actions, then hooks, and enables Snapshot only after that sequence completes.

LOAD-LLF executes top-level forms directly and supplies no whole-IPL restart.  Adding a retained stop alone would therefore leave startup failures without a reliable retry/abort boundary.  An entire IPL retry would repeat filesystem registration and SWANK startup.  A correction needs a defined retry boundary for the failing initialization operation, retained condition/frame inspection, and an explicit skip/abort choice.  Early boot before the remote service exists needs a separate documented failure path.  Test the post-SWANK failure, init-file failure, early/ordinary/late hook failures, restart result, repeated effects, and Snapshot inhibition through recovery.  These findings are source inspection; no startup-recovery implementation has been selected or changed.

[HANDLER-CASE](https://www.lispworks.com/documentation/HyperSpec/Body/m_hand_1.htm) unwinds the failing dynamic context before entering its clause.  [INVOKE-DEBUGGER](https://www.lispworks.com/documentation/HyperSpec/Body/f_invoke.htm) retains that context until a restart transfers control.  [ABORT and related restart functions](https://www.lispworks.com/documentation/HyperSpec/Body/f_abortc.htm) invoke applicable restarts.  Their behavior supports using the retained debugger on the failing startup thread.

Here the faulting thread was the collector and the protected page belonged to the coordinator.  It therefore delivered a memory-fault error to the collector.  ERROR/COPY-LIST attempted allocation while GC was active and panicked with “Allocating during GC!”

### Source-display implementation review

The primary Show Source Code reference is printed pages 212–213, PDF pages 217–218, in the Program Development Utilities manual. Current native metadata stores a pathname and top-level form ordinal, with no retained source body.  Native COMPILE-FILE and the cross-file compiler both read through the existing LOCATION-TRACKING-STREAM.  That stream tracks file positions and line/character coordinates but discards text.  Its READ-CHAR and UNREAD-CHAR methods provide the point at which original consumed text could be retained without rereading a changed file.  PASS1-LAMBDA constructs each source function before transformation, and COPY-FORM copies its plist, which can carry a shared source record through deferred compilation without adding worker-global state.  COMPILE-FILE currently defers the AST and ordinal, and the common backend assembles its debug-info list.  LAP functions have separate native/cross metadata construction paths.  The assembler fills index 14 with instruction starts.  Interpreted functions have a separate metadata method.  These are inspected paths, not source-display implementation. ### Retained file source: reviewed first increment

The Genera Program Development Utilities manual, printed pages 212–213 (PDF pages 217–218), distinguishes displaying source text from source-locator mouse operations.  Its default is the selected frame's function, with an optional compiled function specification.  Reference: https://www.chai.uni-hamburg.de/~moeller/symbolics-info/documentation/Program-Development-Utilities.pdf.  Our current function metadata retains only a file pathname and top-level form number.  Reading that file after an edit cannot establish the executing function's source version.

Review covered both compiler readers, the separate native/cross location-stream implementations, PASS1 lambda construction and AST copying, deferred native compilation, backend metadata, LAP metadata, and the existing runtime readers.  The native capture component already tested character reconstruction, successful unread, comments, Unicode, EOF, and read-time evaluation.  The final recommendation is a source-recording subclass of the existing location stream, without changing ordinary location streams.  A shared helper in the existing native/cross file-compiler module returns the form and one immutable-by-convention vector: #(:SOURCE-TEXT pathname top-level-form-number line character text).  Coordinates identify the captured input's start, which can include leading whitespace or comments.  Each read snapshots the consumed characters before the compiler processes that form.

Bind that record only while processing its top-level form.  PASS1 stores its identity in the lambda plist, which existing AST copying preserves.  Deferred workers read it from their AST rather than depending on a new worker binding.  Native and cross file compilers use the same representation.  Backend and explicit LAP metadata append it at index 15, after the existing instruction-start field at index 14.  DEBUG 1 or higher retains the record.  DEBUG 0 omits it.  Multiple functions from one top-level form share the record, and compiled-file serialization uses the existing vector/string serializer.  No new source registry, external source database, dependency, or compatibility mechanism is needed.

This bounded increment covers file compilation and metadata only.  Ordinary COMPILE and interpreted functions without retained file text continue to report unavailable text.  Listener source capture, optional-name command selection, text rendering, exact function-version selection, source fragments/PC mapping, and source-based operations remain subsequent work.  Generated functions can refer to their generating top-level form, so output must identify that compilation input rather than claim an exact individual lambda span.  Existing callable and source-scope metadata remain unchanged.

Before production acceptance, test exact capture and coordinates, native serial and forced-parallel COMPILE-FILE, DEBUG 0/1/3, shared source identity across nested/generated functions and AST copies, compile-time forms, LAP, compiled-file reload, old function retention through file replacement/redefinition, unrelated concurrent compilations, and moving GC.  Measure retained text size.  Run in Mezzano and preserve the frozen cold source/HOME manifests.  Cross execution and saved-image acceptance require separate recorded tests.

## Throw command: reviewed next increment

Authoritative Genera reference: [Program Development Utilities, Throw](https://www.chai.uni-hamburg.de/~moeller/symbolics-info/documentation/Program-Development-Utilities.pdf#page=235), printed page 229. ### Captured loop storage reproduced and correction reviewed

The revised runtime-sequence DOLIST diagnostic compiled without warnings and completed in 7.92 seconds.  The ordinary control retained its exact descriptor/storage, both reads and shared write.  The loop's current scope retained VALUE's descriptor, but FRAME-LOCALS had no matching storage and its function had no precise closure environment.  Both evaluator reads entered typed UNAVAILABLE-BINDING children, which were inspected, Aborted and released.  The original loop then completed with one cleanup.  Full empty-state/provenance checks passed after coordinator release.  Preserve runtime-loop/native.log, SHA-256 37121efedf62525606b3d6f7baa9ff5dc50e068afcb996b63c118e0d78cd837c.  Test-only metadata records both loaded source/LLF pairs, nineteen test rows and 2268 source files.

The cause is missing metadata for an existing storage location.  LOWER-ENV-FORM allocates TAGBODY-local environment vectors, whereas emitted function debug-info records only the function-level environment pointer/layout.  The original VALUE binding becomes a hidden incoming value after its value enters the vector.  The owning loop's debugger therefore cannot locate that shared cell.  Replacing it with a retained copy would make writes disagree with compiled closures.

Final recommendation after reviewing the front end, both target emitters, compressed location format, frame readers/writers and compiler pipeline: record each TAGBODY-local environment pointer and its current vector layout in one additional common function debug-info field.  Reuse COMPUTE-ENVIRONMENT-LAYOUT-DEBUG-INFO and its existing preservation flag, keeping only the current vector level because parent vectors already have their own records.  The common backend converts pointer variables to their existing binding descriptors.  FRAME-LOCALS resolves those pointers through the existing precise local map and expands the existing environment-index paths.  Reads and writes then use the current shared vector through unchanged READ-FRAME-SLOT/WRITE-FRAME-SLOT.  Preserve the current function/closure layout.  An uninitialized NIL loop pointer supplies no bindings.  This avoids changes to compressed locations, binding descriptor shapes, target instruction emitters, evaluation, closure allocation or executable accesses.

### Inline Throw operand recommendation

Primary reference: [Genera Program Development Utilities](https://www.chai.uni-hamburg.de/~moeller/symbolics-info/documentation/Program-Development-Utilities.pdf#page=235), printed pages 199 and 229.  Object arguments are evaluated forms.  Throw accepts a catch-tag expression and a value expression, and prompts for an omitted value expression.  Existing Mezzano Throw prompts for both operands.

Final recommendation after reviewing command-name recognition, assistance, retained command acceptance/copy/replay, selected-frame reader/evaluator context, HTTP, SWANK and the existing Throw tests: retain the inline operand text as one optional source string.  Recognize the command head before tokenizing its operands.  Assistance must preserve the source while it contains spaces, comments or unfinished quoted forms.  Within the stopped thread's existing evaluation context, read at most two inline forms with read-time evaluation disabled and reject a third form before evaluating either.  Evaluate the tag and value forms through SERVICE-EVALUATE-INPUT, retaining the current history, primary tag, all values, confirmation, child Abort and ordinary unwinding.  Prompt for an omitted tag or values expression.  Copy accepted source and compare it with EQUAL for replay through both native and SWANK entry paths.  HTTP accepts NIL or a string.  Browser rendering uses the existing retained command/input path.

Required tests: existing prompt-only suite; inline tag with prompted values; two inline forms with zero/one/multiple values and heap identities; lexical/dynamic bindings and history; spaces/quoted strings/comments; incomplete source and read-time evaluation rejection; third-form rejection before effects; same-text replay from a distinct string and changed-text rejection; cancellation and child Abort; continuation/cleanup; typed Listener and Display Debugger commands, completion/help, reload, lost replies and subsequent Listener evaluation.  Source preparation is independent of the frozen cold candidate; publication waits for its acceptance and browser handback.

### Inline reader end-marker review

Source review found that SERVICE-THROW passes its input stream as READ's EOF value and stops when READ returns that stream.  A reader macro receives the stream and may return it as its parsed object.  The [READ specification](https://www.lispworks.com/documentation/HyperSpec/Body/f_rd_rd.htm) distinguishes parsed objects from the chosen EOF value.  The [reader algorithm](https://www.lispworks.com/documentation/HyperSpec/Body/02_b.htm) returns the macro function's single value.  SERVICE-EVALUATE already uses a private cons as its EOF marker.

### Return syntax review and SAR64 stepping recommendation

The delegated host-only review checked Genera Program Development Utilities section 5.4.4, printed page 229/PDF 235, and the summary at printed page 242/PDF 248.  The command is bare :Return.  The displayed c-R is its accelerator.  The manual describes caller-count-dependent prompts and confirmation, and does not specify inline Return syntax.  Reference: https://www.chai.uni-hamburg.de/~moeller/symbolics-info/documentation/Program-Development-Utilities.pdf#page=235 .  Mezzano's current one-expression/all-values prompt remains an explicit difference.  Final recommendation: retain that documented behavior while continuing the existing instruction-coverage priority.  An inline Return extension would not resolve the documented Genera difference.

The x86-64 compiler emits SAR64 in fixnum/integer unboxing and arithmetic.  SERVICE-SINGLE-STEP rejects it because its ordinary-instruction list omits SAR64.  The assembler and disassembler already implement it.  Review of Intel's SAL/SAR/SHL/SHR reference specifies signed right shift, six-bit count masking for 64-bit operands, unchanged flags for count zero, cleared overflow for count one, and undefined AF/non-single-bit OF.  Reference: [Intel Volume 2B, printed pages 4-582 through 4-585](https://www.intel.com/content/dam/www/public/us/en/documents/manuals/64-ia-32-architectures-software-developer-vol-2b-manual.pdf#page=584).

Use counts 0, 1, 4, 63, 64, and 65 to distinguish masking and sign extension.  Reuse exact-PC/flags, replay, reference-expiry, moving-GC, code-identity, values, cleanup, and public/private ownership checks.  Add eighty SAR64 cases, for 372 operand cases plus the six existing compiled body walks.  Compile/load prerequisite fixtures and both changed modules ordinarily in the dedicated test guest. ### Trap command semantics: source review

While the shift matrix runs, review of Genera's trap commands confirms activation-specific behavior.  Set Trap On Call stops at the next call made by the current frame, once, and also sets trap on exit for that callee.  Set Trap On Exit targets the current frame, with :All extending it to every frame, and includes THROW through a trapped frame.  References: [Program Development Utilities, printed pages 233–234/PDF 239–240](https://www.chai.uni-hamburg.de/~moeller/symbolics-info/documentation/Program-Development-Utilities.pdf#page=239).  Mezzano's existing TRACE :BREAK installs a wrapper on a named function and affects repeated calls through that definition.  It does not implement these per-activation commands.  Later trap design must examine the existing physical-frame identity, private step/return locations, nonlocal-exit notifications, and four-slot capacity rather than substitute TRACE.  No trap implementation or complete design follows from this source review.

### Caller-location support for exit traps

Review found that FRAME-RETURN-CONTEXT includes scope and unwind restrictions needed for changing control flow.  Exit monitoring needs the caller code location and stack pointer.  The existing physical backtrace walker already derives them from GC metadata, including frameless functions.  Requiring unwind scope would reject valid monitored continuations.

Final recommendation: factor the existing x86-64 backtrace loop into one internal context visitor, preserve MAP-BACKTRACE's one-argument callback API, and add FRAME-RETURN-LOCATION for a selected live frame on its owning thread.  Return caller function/offset/SP or an explicit unavailable reason.  Keep the existing Return/unwind validation unchanged. ### Exit-trap implementation recommendation

Review of the accepted component tests and the physical walker supports continuation identity as caller function object, byte offset, and post-return stack pointer.  A captured frame's FP/PC-slot describes its current suspension and can change when the activation makes another call.  Do not retain those two fields as the activation's long-lived identity.  Keep labels separately.  Tail-call-elided frames have no distinct physical activation.

Final recommendation: implement selected-frame exit trapping and whole-stack Set/Clear using one ordered list per target thread and one private callback point for its innermost pending continuation.  Root that state through the existing point's callback argument and bind it dynamically while delivery runs.  This avoids a separate thread registry, thread slot, exit hook, or one hardware slot per frame.  Existing final thread cleanup removes the last point and its roots.  Merge/reorder active continuation keys using the current physical stack rather than stack-address sorting across prompts or stale captured indices.

Preserve :All's independence from selection.  Include debugger activations in the location inventory.  Report the outermost no-caller activation explicitly rather than silently excluding it or pretending that thread termination is a Lisp return.  Current evidence locates that boundary; delivery there remains unsupported.  Any other unavailable frame must fail preparation before altering the installed point.  Do not use function-name or display filters.  Test actual debugger-prefix and interrupt-return continuations before exposing :All.  The interrupt-return path restores saved RF, so source review identifies a possible coincident-location suppression case.  It is untested and must be measured before selecting a correction.

Factor the existing instruction-trap restart/exit protocol out of its condition factory.  The service can then supply a typed exit condition while retaining the same native interrupted-context, Continue, private Single Step transfer and unwind behavior.  Normal return consumes every pending entry at that same continuation once.  A nonlocal transfer consumes its crossed prefix in one typed condition at the real landing, listing crossed activations in inner-to-outer order.  The manual does not prescribe that batching.  Reuse the existing compiler notification and private-point replacement.  Keep the next outer point pending through an exit stop and arm it after normal continuation.  Abort that unwinds the exit delivery cancels that delivery's remaining state.  Command-child Abort leaves the parent delivery intact.  Test these choices explicitly.

Whole-change review requires coordination with retained Single Step: TF delivery or a CALL-return point can coincide with a pending exit.  Before reporting Single Step, check the current saved PC/SP for a due exit and deliver that exit once.  If the exit point wins first, the existing debugger entry cancels the old step.  Preserve unrelated public/private locations and capacity rejection.  Use a shared service entry decision rather than adding another native trap dispatcher.  Snapshot/replay must retain state and must not rearm from browser rendering or repeated accepted command IDs.

### Rearming callback-slot recommendation

Source review found a capacity requirement for ordered exit traps.  DELIVER-CALLBACK-INSTRUCTION-STEP-BREAKPOINT clears its descriptor before invoking Lisp.  The current component callback installs the next outer point afterward.  Another thread can acquire that released slot between those operations.  The source establishes the gap.  No concurrent failure has been claimed.  Blocking other breakpoint users across a paused debugger or retrying an allocation would obscure the required ownership.

Final recommendation after reviewing the installer, replacement, dispatcher, RF return helper, NLX hook and termination cleanup: add an opt-in rearming callback subtype with the existing fields.  Add a :REARM keyword to the existing callback installer, defaulting to NIL.  Existing six-argument calls keep one-shot delivery.  Replacement preserves the subtype.  A rearming delivery holds its exact slot while invoking Lisp and clears that old descriptor in UNWIND-PROTECT afterward.  Replacing the descriptor atomically in the existing world-stop operation keeps the slot reserved.  Final cleanup of the old descriptor leaves a replacement intact.  An un-rearmed return or nonlocal exit removes the old descriptor and propagates errors.

Whole-change review requires an in-flight distinction: a held descriptor has already fired.  The RF helper must not treat it as a newly armed coincident point, and the NLX hook must not retarget it during callback preparation.  Use one thread-dynamic list of currently delivering rearming descriptors, bound only for callback extent.  A list preserves outer delivery identities through nested callbacks.  A newly replaced descriptor has a different identity and remains eligible.  This needs no new descriptor field, persistent trap registry, global lock, magic address, or fixed extra slot.  Keep the hardware address and ownership data intact.

Before compiling or loading any changed resident function, retain the current INSTALL-CALLBACK-INSTRUCTION-STEP-BREAKPOINT, REPLACE-CALLBACK-INSTRUCTION-STEP-BREAKPOINT, DELIVER-CALLBACK-INSTRUCTION-STEP-BREAKPOINT, and %%DEBUGGER-NLX-ENTRY definitions.  Publish the new subtype, special variable, small delivery predicate and changed resident functions from a reviewed extraction matching the complete CPU source.  Load the RF helper ordinarily.  Keep both earlier publication roots.  Do not change existing record layouts or force ordinary tests into resident allocation.

The bounded tests will characterize the existing one-shot slot release and exercise actual rearming callbacks at zero/two prompts.  A callback barrier with all four slots occupied must reject a competing installation, then replace its own point without acquiring a fifth slot.  Verify exact entry and outer-return landings, moving GC, unchanged code, original values and cleanup.  Retain a coincident public point and observe flags at the typed exit debugger's return: an in-flight old point preserves RF, while a fresh matching replacement remains eligible.  Test callback Abort and termination, cancellation before ownership, and nested callbacks with both in-flight points present.  Run existing hardware, retained-step and prefix cases afterward, with full source/compiled/native/protected/asset guards. ### Inherited structure slot order diagnosis

Rearming publication compiled without warnings.  The legacy case passed.  The first rearming ARM entered a child type error before installation: the descriptor's OFFSET contained the callback argument structure.  The coordinator then expired while waiting for that ARM command.  Both retained conditions, stacks, restarts, scalar state and direct constructor probes are preserved under rearming-slot/retry-2.  This is an implementation failure, not a breakpoint-capacity result.

The direct seven-argument constructors distinguish the cause.  The existing callback constructor returns the expected named values.  The new subtype constructor writes them according to a rearranged layout.  Native CLASS-SLOTS enumerates callback and argument before the inherited fields.  Their encoded locations 768 and 896 represent byte offsets 48 and 56.  COMPUTE-DEFSTRUCT-SLOTS discards those locations and assigns new offsets in enumeration order.  The subtype therefore places callback at byte offset zero, argument at eight, function at forty, and offset at forty-eight.  The compiled parent OFFSET accessor still reads byte offset eight, so it returns the callback argument.

Final recommendation after reviewing DEFSTRUCT, class conversion and layout creation: sort a copied inherited slot-definition list by physical byte offset before computing the included layout.  Use a stable sort and the existing LOCATION-OFFSET reader.  Keep the class's own slot list intact.  This corrects the shared inheritance algorithm and keeps parent accessors valid without changing the rearming design.  Source: system/defstruct.lisp COMPUTE-DEFSTRUCT-SLOTS and system/file-compiler.lisp CONVERT-STRUCTURE-CLASS-TO-STRUCTURE-DEFINITION.  CLASS-SLOTS enumeration currently puts direct slots ahead of inherited slots after class finalization.

Test an independent four-level structure family with distinct positional values, read-only fields, packed integers, alignment and fixed vectors.  Finalize parent classes before defining children, compile and load the definitions, check every parent/child accessor and SLOT-VALUE, preserve byte offsets, and repeat after moving GC.  Run existing structure-layout and compiled structure-load tests.  Preserve the failed rearming publication and old resident function roots.  Recompile the new rearming subtype only after this core correction passes, then repeat the complete rearming tests.  No result from the failed run constitutes acceptance of the new capability.
